examples.note: **Its** refers to the dog's tail.

examples.text: **Our** team won the match.
examples.urdu: ہماری ٹیم میچ جیت گئی۔
examples.note: **Our** shows our possession.

examples.text: Where are **their** books?
examples.urdu: ان کی کتابیں کہاں ہیں؟
examples.note: **Their** refers to their possession.

commonMistakes.urdu: کتے نے اپنی دم ہلائی۔
commonMistakes.note: **Its** is possessive; **it's** is a contraction of 'it is'.

commonMistakes.urdu: یہ میرا گھر ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **my** before a noun; **mine** stands alone.

commonMistakes.wrong: She lost **his** purse. (referring to her own)
commonMistakes.urdu: اس نے اپنا پرس کھو دیا۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **her** for a female possessor.

commonMistakes.urdu: کیا یہ آپ کی کتاب ہے؟
commonMistakes.note: Use the possessive form **your** before a noun.

commonMistakes.urdu: وہ اپنے ملک سے محبت کرتے ہیں۔
commonMistakes.note: **Their** is possessive; **there** refers to a place.

types.name: Quantifiers
types.description: Quantifiers indicate the amount or quantity of a noun.
types.urduExplanation: مقداری الفاظ کسی اسم کی مقدار یا تعداد کو ظاہر کرتے ہیں۔
types.exampleWords: some, any, much, many, few, little, a lot of, several
rules: 1: Use **some** in positive sentences and **any** in negative/question sentences.
2: Use **many** with countable nouns and **much** with uncountable nouns.
3: Use **few** (negative sense) and **a few** (positive sense) with countable nouns.
4: Use **little** (negative sense) and **a little** (positive sense) with uncountable nouns.
5: Use **a lot of** or **lots of** with both countable and uncountable nouns.
6: Use **several** for a number that is more than two but not many.
ruleExamples:
I have **some** milk.
Do you have **any** milk? > Positive vs. Question: **some/any**.

I have **many** friends.
I don't have **much** time. > Countable vs. Uncountable: **many/much**.

He has **few** friends. (Not many)
He has **a few** friends. (Some) > Countable quantity: **few/a few**.

There is **little** water. (Not much)
There is **a little** water. (Some) > Uncountable quantity: **little/a little**.

I have **a lot of** work.
There are **a lot of** books. > Both types: **a lot of**.

He has written **several** books.
**Several** people were injured. > More than two: **several**.

examples.text: I have **some** milk.
examples.urdu: میرے پاس کچھ دودھ ہے۔
examples.note: **Some** is used in positive sentences.

examples.note: **A few** means a small number but enough.

examples.note: **A lot of** works with uncountable nouns.

commonMistakes.note: Use **much** with uncountable nouns like money.

commonMistakes.note: Use **any** in negative sentences.

commonMistakes.urdu: اس کے پاس چند کتابیں ہیں۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **a few** with countable nouns.

commonMistakes.urdu: جگ میں تھوڑا سا پانی ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **little** with uncountable nouns like water.

types.name: Numbers and Distributives
types.description: Numbers indicate exact quantity, while distributives refer to individual members of a group.
types.urduExplanation: اعداد صحیح تعداد کو ظاہر کرتے ہیں، جبکہ تقسیم کرنے والے الفاظ کسی گروہ کے انفرادی ارکان کی طرف اشارہ کرتے ہیں۔
types.exampleWords: one, two, first, second, each, every, either, neither
rules: 1: Use **cardinal numbers** (one, two) for counting.
2: Use **ordinal numbers** (first, second) for order or position.
3: Use **each** when referring to individuals in a small, specific group.
4: Use **every** when referring to all members of a large, general group.
5: Use **either** for one of two and **neither** for none of two.
6: Distributives are usually followed by a singular verb.
ruleExamples:
I have **two** sisters.
There are **ten** students. > Counting: **one, two...**.

He came **first** in the race.
This is the **second** time. > Order: **first, second...**.

**Each** student got a prize.
**Each** of the two boys was tall. > Specific individuals: **each**.

**Every** child loves toys.
I go there **every** day. > General group: **every**.

You can take **either** path.
**Neither** answer is correct. > One of two / None of two.

**Each** student **is** present.
**Neither** plan **works**. > Singular verb rule.

examples.text: I have **two** sisters.
examples.urdu: میری دو بہنیں ہیں۔
examples.note: **Two** is a cardinal number.

examples.text: He came **first** in the race.
examples.urdu: وہ ریس میں پہلے نمبر پر آیا۔
examples.note: **First** is an ordinal number.

examples.text: **Each** student got a prize.
examples.urdu: ہر طالب علم کو انعام ملا۔
examples.note: **Each** refers to individual students.

examples.text: **Every** child loves toys.
examples.urdu: ہر بچہ کھلونوں سے محبت کرتا ہے۔
examples.note: **Every** refers to children in general.

examples.text: **Neither** answer is correct.
examples.urdu: کوئی بھی جواب صحیح نہیں ہے۔
examples.note: **Neither** means none of the two.

commonMistakes.urdu: ہر طالب علم کو انعام ملا۔
commonMistakes.note: **Each** is followed by a singular noun.

commonMistakes.wrong: **Every** of the two boys is here.
commonMistakes.right: **Each** of the two boys is here.
commonMistakes.urdu: دونوں لڑکوں میں سے ہر ایک یہاں ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **each** for a small, specific number like two.

commonMistakes.urdu: ان میں سے کوئی نہیں آ رہا۔
commonMistakes.note: Distributives like **neither** take a singular verb.

commonMistakes.wrong: He is the **one** boy in the line. (position)
commonMistakes.right: He is the **first** boy in the line.
commonMistakes.urdu: وہ لائن میں پہلا لڑکا ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Use ordinal numbers for position.

commonMistakes.urdu: مجھے ان میں سے ہر کتاب پسند ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **each** when followed by 'of'.

types.name: Interrogative Determiners
types.description: Interrogative determiners are used to ask questions about a noun.
types.urduExplanation: سوالیہ ڈٹرمینرز کسی اسم کے بارے میں سوال پوچھنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔
types.exampleWords: which, what, whose
rules: 1: Use **which** when there is a limited choice.
2: Use **what** when asking for general information (unlimited choice).
3: Use **whose** to ask about possession.
4: Interrogative determiners must be followed immediately by a noun.
5: Do not confuse interrogative determiners with interrogative pronouns.
ruleExamples:
**Which** color do you prefer, red or blue?
**Which** way should we go? > Limited choice: **which**.

**What** time is it?
**What** subjects are you studying? > General info: **what**.

**Whose** bag is this?
**Whose** car are we taking? > Possession: **whose**.

**Which** book (noun) is yours?
**Whose** pen (noun) is this? > Followed by noun.

**Which** is yours? (Pronoun)
**Which** book is yours? (Determiner) > Determiner vs. Pronoun.

examples.text: **Which** color do you prefer?
examples.urdu: آپ کو کون سا رنگ پسند ہے؟
examples.note: **Which** is used for a limited choice.

examples.text: **What** time is it?

examples.note: **What** asks for general information.

examples.text: **What** subjects are you studying?
examples.urdu: آپ کون سے مضامین پڑھ رہے ہیں؟
examples.note: **What** modifies the noun 'subjects'.

commonMistakes.wrong: **What** way should we go, left or right?
commonMistakes.right: **Which** way should we go, left or right?
commonMistakes.urdu: ہمیں کس راستے پر جانا چاہیے، بائیں یا دائیں؟
commonMistakes.note: Use **which** for limited choices.

commonMistakes.urdu: یہ کس کا قلم ہے؟
commonMistakes.note: As a determiner, **whose** must be followed by a noun.

commonMistakes.right: **Which** one do you like? (or **Which** book do you like?)
commonMistakes.urdu: آپ کو کون سا پسند ہے؟
commonMistakes.note: A determiner needs a noun or 'one' to modify.

commonMistakes.wrong: **What** book is yours? (when pointing to two)
commonMistakes.urdu: آپ کی کتاب کون سی ہے؟
commonMistakes.note: Use **which** when the options are known or limited.

commonMistakes.urdu: یہ کس کا بیگ ہے؟
commonMistakes.note: **Whose** is possessive; **who's** is 'who is'.

quiz.question: I have ___ umbrella in my bag.
quiz.explanation: Use **an** before singular countable nouns starting with a vowel sound (u in umbrella). **Urdu:** لفظ 'umbrella' وول (vowel) آواز سے شروع ہوتا ہے، اس لیے اس سے پہلے 'an' استعمال ہوگا۔

quiz.question: He is ___ honest man.
quiz.explanation: Use **an** because 'honest' starts with a vowel sound (h is silent). **Urdu:** لفظ 'honest' میں 'h' خاموش ہے اور یہ وول آواز سے شروع ہوتا ہے، اس لیے 'an' استعمال ہوگا۔

quiz.question: ___ sun rises in the east.
quiz.explanation: Use **the** for unique objects like the sun. **Urdu:** سورج جیسی منفرد چیزوں کے لیے 'the' استعمال کیا جاتا ہے۔

quiz.question: He is ___ tallest boy in the class.
quiz.explanation: Use **the** before superlative adjectives (tallest). **Urdu:** صفت کی تیسری ڈگری (superlative) سے پہلے ہمیشہ 'the' لگایا جاتا ہے۔

quiz.question: I don't have ___ money in my pocket.
quiz.explanation: Use **any** in negative sentences with uncountable nouns like money. **Urdu:** منفی جملوں میں 'any' استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

quiz.question: How ___ time do we have left?
quiz.explanation: Use **much** with uncountable nouns like time. **Urdu:** غیر شمار شدہ اسم (uncountable nouns) جیسے وقت کے لیے 'much' استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

quiz.question: There are ___ students in the library.
quiz.explanation: Use **many** with plural countable nouns like students. **Urdu:** شمار شدہ اسم (countable nouns) کی جمع کے لیے 'many' استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

quiz.question: I have ___ friends, so I am never lonely.
quiz.explanation: **A few** has a positive meaning (some), while **few** means almost none. **Urdu:** 'A few' کا مطلب ہے 'کچھ' (مثبت معنوں میں)۔

quiz.question: Can you give me ___ water?
quiz.explanation: Use **some** for uncountable nouns in requests or positive sentences. **Urdu:** درخواست یا مثبت جملوں میں غیر شمار شدہ اسم کے لیے 'some' استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

quiz.question: ___ book on the table is mine.
quiz.explanation: Use **this** for a singular noun nearby. **Urdu:** قریب کی ایک چیز کے لیے 'this' استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

quiz.question: ___ students over there are playing football.
quiz.explanation: Use **those** for plural nouns at a distance. **Urdu:** دور کی زیادہ چیزوں کے لیے 'those' استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

quiz.question: ___ of the two sisters is a doctor.
quiz.explanation: Use **each** when referring to a small, specific number like two. **Urdu:** دو یا دو سے زیادہ مخصوص افراد میں سے ہر ایک کے لیے 'each' استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

quiz.question: ___ answer is correct; both are wrong.
quiz.explanation: Use **neither** to reject both options. **Urdu:** جب دونوں آپشنز غلط ہوں تو 'neither' استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

quiz.question: I need to buy ___ milk.
quiz.explanation: Use **some** with uncountable nouns in positive sentences. **Urdu:** مثبت جملوں میں 'some' استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

quiz.question: She is ___ university student.
quiz.explanation: Use **a** because 'university' starts with a consonant sound (yoo). **Urdu:** اگرچہ 'university' 'u' سے شروع ہوتا ہے، لیکن اس کی آواز کونسوننٹ (consonant) ہے، اس لیے 'a' آئے گا۔

practice.explanation: Use **the** before superlative adjectives (tallest). **Urdu:** صفت کی تیسری ڈگری (superlative) سے پہلے ہمیشہ 'the' لگایا جاتا ہے۔

practice.question: I don't have ___ money in my pocket.
practice.explanation: Use **any** in negative sentences with uncountable nouns like money. **Urdu:** منفی جملوں میں 'any' استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

content.introduction: An interjection is a word or short phrase used to express sudden emotion, such as surprise, joy, pain, or excitement.
content.urduExplanation: حرفِ ندا وہ لفظ یا مختصر جملہ ہے جو اچانک جذبات جیسے حیرانی، خوشی، درد یا جوش کے اظہار کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے۔
content.englishExplanation: Interjections are unique because they are grammatically independent from the rest of the sentence. They are mainly used in spoken English and informal writing to add emotional depth and naturalness. In competitive exams, they are important for understanding dialogue and narrative passages, as well as for correct punctuation (exclamation marks vs. commas).

examples.text: Wow!, Alas!, Hurrah!, Bravo!, Hello!, Ouch!, Hey!, Hush!
examples.note: Common examples of interjections.

types.name: Interjection of Joy
types.description: These interjections express sudden happiness, pleasure, or excitement.
types.urduExplanation: حرفِ ندا برائے خوشی وہ الفاظ ہیں جو اچانک خوشی، مسرت یا جوش کے اظہار کے لیے استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔
types.exampleWords: Hurrah, Wow, Yay, Yippee, Ha-ha
rules: 1: Use **Hurrah** to celebrate a victory or achievement.
2: Use **Wow** to show sudden delight or pleasure.
3: Use **Yay** or **Yippee** to express excitement, especially among friends.
4: Use **Ha-ha** to express joy accompanied by laughter.
5: Always use an exclamation mark (!) to show the intensity of the joy.
ruleExamples:
**Hurrah!** We won the match.
**Hurrah!** The holidays have started. > Celebration: **Hurrah!**.

**Wow!** This place is beautiful.
**Wow!** What a pleasant surprise. > Delight: **Wow!**.

**Yay!** We are going to the picnic.
**Yippee!** I got the first prize. > Excitement: **Yay!/Yippee!**.

**Ha-ha!** That was a funny joke.
**Ha-ha!** I can't stop laughing. > Laughter: **Ha-ha!**.

**Hurrah!** Our team is at the top.
**Wow!** You look great today. > Punctuation rule.

examples.text: **Hurrah!** We won the match.
examples.urdu: ہاہا! ہم میچ جیت گئے۔
examples.note: **Hurrah** shows the joy of victory.

examples.text: **Wow!** This place is beautiful.
examples.urdu: واہ! یہ جگہ خوبصورت ہے۔
examples.note: **Wow** shows delight.

examples.text: **Yay!** We are going to the picnic.
examples.urdu: واہ! ہم پکنک پر جا رہے ہیں۔
examples.note: **Yay** shows excitement.

examples.text: **Yippee!** I got the first prize.
examples.urdu: ہمارے! مجھے پہلا انعام ملا۔
examples.note: **Yippee** shows extreme happiness.

examples.text: **Ha-ha!** That was a funny joke.
examples.urdu: ہاہا! وہ ایک مضحکہ خیز لطیفہ تھا۔
examples.note: **Ha-ha** shows joy with laughter.

commonMistakes.urdu: ہاہا! ہم میچ جیت گئے۔
commonMistakes.note: Don't use a sorrowful interjection for a happy occasion.

commonMistakes.wrong: **Hurrah** we won the match. (without exclamation mark)
commonMistakes.urdu: ہاہا! ہم میچ جیت گئے۔
commonMistakes.note: Interjections of strong emotion need an exclamation mark.

commonMistakes.urdu: واہ! میں آج بہت خوش ہوں۔
commonMistakes.note: **Ouch** is for pain, not joy.

commonMistakes.urdu: واہ! میں نے امتحان پاس کر لیا۔
commonMistakes.note: Use an exclamation mark for strong excitement instead of a comma.

commonMistakes.urdu: افسوس! میں اداس ہوں۔
commonMistakes.note: Laughter interjections are for joy only.

types.name: Interjection of Sorrow
types.description: These interjections express sadness, grief, regret, or disappointment.
types.urduExplanation: حرفِ ندا برائے افسوس وہ الفاظ ہیں جو اداسی، غم، پچھتاوے یا مایوسی کے اظہار کے لیے استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔
types.exampleWords: Alas, Oh, Ah, Oh no, Woe
rules: 1: Use **Alas** to express deep grief or regret.
2: Use **Oh no** to show disappointment or bad news.
3: Use **Ah** to show pity or sadness.
4: Use **Oh** to express a sudden realization of sorrow.
5: These interjections are usually followed by an exclamation mark to show the depth of the feeling.
ruleExamples:
**Alas!** He is no more.
**Alas!** I failed the exam. > Deep grief: **Alas!**.

**Oh no!** I lost my keys.
**Oh no!** The shop is closed. > Disappointment: **Oh no!**.

**Ah!** What a pity.
**Ah!** The poor man is suffering. > Pity: **Ah!**.

**Oh!** I am so sorry for your loss.
**Oh!** That is terrible news. > Realization of sorrow: **Oh!**.

**Alas!** The old man died.
**Oh no!** I forgot my wallet. > Punctuation rule.

examples.text: **Alas!** He is no more.
examples.urdu: افسوس! وہ اب نہیں رہے۔
examples.note: **Alas** shows deep grief.

examples.text: **Oh no!** I lost my keys.
examples.urdu: اوہ نہیں! میں نے اپنی چابیاں کھو دیں۔
examples.note: **Oh no** shows disappointment.

examples.text: **Ah!** What a pity.
examples.urdu: آہ! کتنے افسوس کی بات ہے۔
examples.note: **Ah** shows pity.

examples.text: **Oh!** I am so sorry for your loss.
examples.urdu: اوہ! مجھے آپ کے نقصان پر بہت افسوس ہے۔
examples.note: **Oh** shows sympathy and sorrow.

examples.text: **Woe!** Woe is me.
examples.urdu: ہائے افسوس! میری شامت آگئی۔
examples.note: **Woe** is a literary interjection for grief.

commonMistakes.urdu: افسوس! میرا دوست فوت ہو گیا۔
commonMistakes.note: Use sorrowful interjections for sad news.

commonMistakes.urdu: ہاہا! میں خوش ہوں۔
commonMistakes.note: **Alas** is only for sadness.

commonMistakes.urdu: اوہ نہیں! میرے پیسے کھو گئے۔
commonMistakes.note: **Wow** is for delight, not loss.

commonMistakes.urdu: افسوس! وہ مر گیا ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Strong sorrow needs an exclamation mark.

commonMistakes.urdu: اوہ! حادثہ بہت خوفناک تھا۔
commonMistakes.note: Don't use joy interjections for accidents.

types.name: Interjection of Surprise
types.description: These interjections express sudden amazement, wonder, or shock.
types.urduExplanation: حرفِ ندا برائے حیرت وہ الفاظ ہیں جو اچانک حیرانی، تعجب یا صدمے کے اظہار کے لیے استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔
types.exampleWords: What, Ha, Oh, Gosh, My goodness, Wow
rules: 1: Use **What** to show disbelief or shock.
2: Use **Ha** to show a sudden discovery or surprise.
3: Use **Gosh** or **My goodness** for mild surprise or amazement.
4: Use **Wow** to show surprise mixed with admiration.
5: Use **Oh** for a sudden shock or unexpected news.
ruleExamples:
**What!** You failed again?
**What!** Is it already 10 PM? > Shock: **What!**.

**Ha!** I found you.
**Ha!** So that's how it works. > Discovery: **Ha!**.

**Gosh!** That's a huge cake.
**My goodness!** You have grown so tall. > Amazement: **Gosh!**.

**Wow!** Did you really do that?
**Wow!** Look at that view. > Admiration/Surprise: **Wow!**.

**Oh!** I didn't see you there.
**Oh!** Is that true? > Unexpected news: **Oh!**.

examples.text: **What!** You failed again?
examples.urdu: کیا! تم دوبارہ فیل ہو گئے؟
examples.note: **What** shows disbelief.

examples.text: **Ha!** I found you.
examples.urdu: ہاہا! میں نے تمہیں ڈھونڈ لیا۔
examples.note: **Ha** shows the surprise of discovery.

examples.text: **My goodness!** You have grown so tall.
examples.urdu: میرے خدا! تم اتنے لمبے ہو گئے ہو۔
examples.note: **My goodness** shows amazement.

examples.text: **Wow!** Did you really do that?
examples.urdu: واہ! کیا تم نے واقعی یہ کیا؟
examples.note: **Wow** shows surprise and admiration.

examples.text: **Gosh!** That's a huge cake.
examples.urdu: اوہ! یہ ایک بہت بڑا کیک ہے۔
examples.note: **Gosh** shows mild surprise.

commonMistakes.urdu: واہ! آپ نے دس لاکھ ڈالر جیت لیے۔
commonMistakes.note: Use surprise/joy interjections for good news.

commonMistakes.urdu: کیا! تم یہاں ہو؟
commonMistakes.note: Interjections of shock need an exclamation mark.

commonMistakes.wrong: **Hurrah!** I didn't know you were coming.
commonMistakes.right: **Oh!** I didn't know you were coming.
commonMistakes.urdu: اوہ! مجھے نہیں معلوم تھا کہ تم آ رہے ہو۔
commonMistakes.note: **Oh** is better for sudden realization/surprise.

commonMistakes.urdu: واہ! یہ ایک خوبصورت پینٹنگ ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: **Ouch** is for pain, not beauty.

commonMistakes.urdu: کیا! کیا یہ واقعی سچ ہے؟
commonMistakes.note: **What** is better for questioning surprise.

types.name: Interjection of Approval or Praise
types.description: These interjections express appreciation, admiration, or encouragement for someone's work or behavior.
types.urduExplanation: حرفِ ندا برائے شاباش وہ الفاظ ہیں جو کسی کے کام یا رویے کی تعریف، تحسین یا حوصلہ افزائی کے لیے استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔
types.exampleWords: Bravo, Well done, Splendid, Good, Brilliant
rules: 1: Use **Bravo** to applaud a great performance or act.
2: Use **Well done** to encourage someone who has finished a task successfully.
3: Use **Splendid** or **Brilliant** to show high admiration for something excellent.
4: Use **Good** for mild approval or agreement.
5: These are often used to boost someone's confidence.
ruleExamples:
**Bravo!** You played exceptionally well.
**Bravo!** That was a courageous act. > Applaud: **Bravo!**.

**Well done!** You passed with flying colors.
**Well done!** Keep it up. > Encouragement: **Well done!**.

**Splendid!** Your idea is perfect.
**Brilliant!** That's a great solution. > High admiration: **Splendid!/Brilliant!**.

**Good!** Now we can move forward.
**Good!** I agree with you. > Mild approval: **Good!**.

**Bravo!** You made us proud.
**Well done!** I knew you could do it. > Confidence boost.

examples.text: **Bravo!** You played exceptionally well.
examples.urdu: شاباش! تم نے غیر معمولی طور پر اچھا کھیلا۔
examples.note: **Bravo** shows high praise.

examples.text: **Well done!** You passed with flying colors.
examples.urdu: بہت خوب! تم نے شاندار کامیابی حاصل کی۔
examples.note: **Well done** encourages the person.

examples.text: **Splendid!** Your idea is perfect.
examples.urdu: شاندار! آپ کا خیال بہترین ہے۔
examples.note: **Splendid** shows high admiration.

examples.text: **Brilliant!** That's a great solution.
examples.urdu: بہت شاندار! یہ ایک بہترین حل ہے۔
examples.note: **Brilliant** shows appreciation for intelligence.

examples.text: **Good!** Now we can move forward.
examples.urdu: اچھا! اب ہم آگے بڑھ سکتے ہیں۔
examples.note: **Good** shows mild approval.

commonMistakes.right: **Well done!** You did a great job.
commonMistakes.urdu: بہت خوب! تم نے بہت اچھا کام کیا۔
commonMistakes.note: Use praise interjections for achievements.

commonMistakes.urdu: شاباش! تم نے انعام جیتا۔
commonMistakes.note: **Ouch** is for pain.

commonMistakes.urdu: شاباش! تم نے کر دکھایا۔
commonMistakes.note: Strong praise needs an exclamation mark.

commonMistakes.urdu: شاندار! تم بہت ذہین ہو۔
commonMistakes.note: **Brilliant** is better for praising intelligence.

commonMistakes.urdu: شاندار! تم نے بہت خوبصورتی سے گایا۔
commonMistakes.note: Don't use disappointment interjections for praise.

types.name: Interjection of Greeting and Attention
types.description: These interjections are used to address someone, start a conversation, or call for attention.
types.urduExplanation: حرفِ ندا برائے سلام و توجہ وہ الفاظ ہیں جو کسی کو مخاطب کرنے، بات چیت شروع کرنے یا توجہ حاصل کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔
types.exampleWords: Hello, Hi, Hey, Listen, Look, Behold, Hush
rules: 1: Use **Hello** or **Hi** for a standard greeting.
2: Use **Hey** to get someone's attention informally.
3: Use **Listen** or **Look** to direct someone's focus to something specific.
4: Use **Behold** (literary) to call attention to something remarkable.
5: Use **Hush** or **Shh** to call for silence.
ruleExamples:
**Hello!** How are you today?
**Hi!** Nice to see you. > Greeting: **Hello!/Hi!**.

**Hey!** Can you help me?
**Hey!** Watch where you are going. > Attention: **Hey!**.

**Listen!** I have something important to tell you.
**Look!** There is a rainbow. > Focus: **Listen!/Look!**.

**Behold!** The king has arrived.
**Behold!** A miracle has happened. > Remarkable attention: **Behold!**.

**Hush!** The baby is sleeping.
**Shh!** Be quiet in the library. > Silence: **Hush!/Shh!**.

examples.text: **Hello!** How are you today?
examples.urdu: ہیلو! آج آپ کیسے ہیں؟
examples.note: **Hello** is a standard greeting.

examples.text: **Hey!** Can you help me?
examples.urdu: ارے! کیا آپ میری مدد کر سکتے ہیں؟
examples.note: **Hey** calls for attention.

examples.text: **Listen!** I have something important to tell you.
examples.urdu: سنو! مجھے تمہیں ایک اہم بات بتانی ہے۔
examples.note: **Listen** directs focus to the speaker.

examples.text: **Look!** There is a rainbow.
examples.urdu: دیکھو! وہاں ایک دھنک ہے۔
examples.note: **Look** directs focus to an object.

examples.text: **Hush!** The baby is sleeping.
examples.urdu: خاموش! بچہ سو رہا ہے۔
examples.note: **Hush** calls for silence.

commonMistakes.urdu: ہیلو! آپ کیسے ہیں؟
commonMistakes.note: Use greetings to start a conversation.

commonMistakes.urdu: ارے! کیا آپ مجھے سن سکتے ہیں؟
commonMistakes.note: Use attention interjections to call someone.

commonMistakes.urdu: دیکھو! اسے دیکھو۔
commonMistakes.note: **Hush** is for silence, not for showing something.

commonMistakes.urdu: ہیلو! آپ کیسے ہیں؟
commonMistakes.note: Greetings usually take an exclamation mark or comma.

commonMistakes.urdu: سنو! میری بات سنو۔
commonMistakes.note: **Ouch** is for pain, not for calling attention.

content.introduction: A noun is the name of a person, place, animal, thing, substance, or idea.
content.urduExplanation: کسی شخص، جگہ، جانور، چیز، مادے یا خیال کے نام کو اسم یعنی Noun کہتے ہیں۔
content.englishExplanation: The main noun categories in this lesson are proper, common, collective, abstract, countable, uncountable, material, and compound nouns. A noun may belong to more than one category: information is both common and uncountable, while Islamabad is both proper and countable in some contexts. Always judge the noun from its use in the sentence.

types.name: Proper Noun
types.description: A Proper Noun is the special name of a particular person, place, day, country, or institution.
types.urduExplanation: اسمِ خاص کسی خاص شخص، جگہ، دن، ملک یا ادارے کا مخصوص نام ہوتا ہے۔

examples.text: Fatima Jinnah was the sister of Mohammad Ali Jinnah.
examples.urdu: فاطمہ جناح، محمد علی جناح کی بہن تھیں۔
examples.note: Fatima Jinnah and Mohammad Ali Jinnah are specific people, so they are Proper Nouns and begin with capital letters.

examples.text: The Indus River flows through Pakistan.
examples.urdu: دریائے سندھ پاکستان سے ہو کر گزرتا ہے۔
examples.note: Indus River is the specific name of a river, and Pakistan is the specific name of a country; both are Proper Nouns.

examples.text: The Faisal Mosque is beautiful.
examples.urdu: فیصل مسجد خوبصورت ہے۔
examples.note: Faisal Mosque names one particular mosque, so it is a Proper Noun and begins with capital letters.

examples.text: The commission will meet on Monday in Quetta.
examples.urdu: کمیشن پیر کے روز کوئٹہ میں اجلاس کرے گا۔
examples.note: Monday and Quetta are specific names of a day and a place, so both are Proper Nouns.

rules: Always begin a **Proper Noun** with a **capital letter**.
A Proper Noun names one **specific person, place, day, country, or institution**.
Do not use **a** or **an** before most Proper Nouns.

commonMistakes.wrong: I will meet you on monday.
commonMistakes.right: I will meet you on Monday.
commonMistakes.urdu: میں آپ سے پیر کے روز ملوں گا۔
commonMistakes.note: Days and months are Proper Nouns, so they begin with capital letters.

commonMistakes.urdu: میں نے کل ایک کتاب خریدی۔
commonMistakes.note: Book is a Common Noun here because it does not name one specific book; it should be lowercase.

commonMistakes.urdu: میں کراچی گیا۔
commonMistakes.note: Karachi already gives the specific city name, so city is unnecessary in ordinary usage. The city of Karachi is also correct when emphasis is needed.

commonMistakes.urdu: علی میرا دوست ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Most Proper Nouns do not take a or an because Ali is already a specific name.

practice.question: Which word is a proper noun in “The students visited Taxila”?
practice.explanation: Taxila is the specific name of a place.

practice.question: Choose the correctly capitalized form.
practice.explanation: The name of the subject is written as Pakistan Studies.

quiz.question: Which is a proper noun in “Ayesha visited Lahore”?
quiz.explanation: Ayesha is a specific name; Lahore is also proper.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form.
quiz.explanation: Pakistan begins with a capital letter.

quiz.question: Which contains only proper nouns?
quiz.explanation: Karachi and Monday are specific names.

quiz.question: Which noun is proper in “The Indus River flows”?
quiz.explanation: Indus River names one particular river.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: CSS is an official abbreviation written in capitals.

ruleExamples: **Islamabad** is the capital of Pakistan.
**Monday** is the first day of the examination.
**Ali** is my friend.
types.exampleWords: Rashid, Quetta, Monday, Pakistan, Supreme Court

types.name: Common Noun
types.description: A Common Noun is a general name given to every person, place, animal, or thing of the same class or kind.
types.urduExplanation: اسمِ عام ایک ہی قسم کے عام شخص، جگہ، جانور یا چیز کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا نام ہے۔

examples.text: A boy is running on the road.
examples.urdu: ایک لڑکا سڑک پر دوڑ رہا ہے۔
examples.note: Boy and road are Common Nouns because they name a general person and place, not specific names.

examples.text: The teacher is in the classroom.
examples.urdu: استاد کلاس روم میں ہے۔
examples.note: Teacher and classroom are Common Nouns. The article the makes these general nouns specific in this context.

examples.text: The student is reading a book.
examples.urdu: طالب علم ایک کتاب پڑھ رہا ہے۔
examples.note: Student and book are Common Nouns. Student is the subject, and book is the object of reading.

examples.text: The river passes through the town.
examples.urdu: دریا قصبے سے گزرتا ہے۔
examples.note: River and town are Common Nouns because they name general kinds of places or things.

rules: A **Common Noun** names a **general person, place, animal, or thing**.
Use **a** or **an** with one **singular countable Common Noun** when needed.
Use **the** when the context makes a Common Noun **specific**.

commonMistakes.urdu: میں نے کل ایک کتاب خریدی۔
commonMistakes.note: Book is a Common Noun, so it normally begins with a lowercase letter.

commonMistakes.urdu: طالب علم پڑھ رہا ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Student is a Common Noun. It is not capitalized merely because it follows the article the.

commonMistakes.urdu: میں نے ایک کتاب خریدی۔
commonMistakes.note: A singular countable Common Noun normally needs a determiner such as a, an, the, my, or this.

commonMistakes.urdu: مجھے کچھ پانی چاہیے۔
commonMistakes.note: Water is normally an Uncountable Noun, so a or an is not used directly before it.

commonMistakes.wrong: There are many childs in the park.
commonMistakes.right: There are many children in the park.
commonMistakes.urdu: پارک میں بہت سے بچے ہیں۔
commonMistakes.note: Child has the irregular plural form children, not childs.

practice.question: Which word is a common noun in “The officer read the report”?
practice.explanation: Officer is a general name for a person.

practice.question: Choose the correct sentence.
practice.explanation: Book is singular and countable, so it needs a.

quiz.question: Which is common in “The teacher entered”?
quiz.explanation: Teacher is a general name.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: The singular candidate takes works.

quiz.question: Which uses a common noun?
quiz.explanation: Child is a general name.

quiz.question: Choose the correct article.
quiz.explanation: Book is singular and countable.

quiz.question: Which is common in “The doctor examined Ali”?
quiz.explanation: Doctor is a general profession.

ruleExamples: The **boy** goes to **school**.
A **candidate** submitted an application.
The **book** on the table is mine.
types.exampleWords: boy, school, hospital, book, river

types.name: Collective Noun
types.description: A Collective Noun names a group of people, animals, or things as one unit.
types.urduExplanation: اسمِ مجموعہ لوگوں، جانوروں یا چیزوں کے ایسے گروہ کا نام ہے جسے ایک اکائی سمجھا جائے۔

examples.text: The committee approved the plan.
examples.urdu: کمیٹی نے منصوبے کی منظوری دی۔
examples.note: Committee names a group acting as one unit, so it is a Collective Noun. It takes the singular verb approved in the past tense.

examples.text: The team won the match.
examples.urdu: ٹیم نے میچ جیت لیا۔
examples.note: Team names several people as one group, so it is a Collective Noun. It acts as one unit here.

examples.text: The jury reached a decision.
examples.urdu: جیوری ایک فیصلے پر پہنچی۔
examples.note: Jury names a group of people. It is singular here because the jury reached one decision as a unit.

examples.text: The staff are checking their files.
examples.urdu: عملہ اپنی فائلیں چیک کر رہا ہے۔
examples.note: Staff is a Collective Noun. It takes are here because the members are acting separately.

rules: A **Collective Noun** names a **group** of people, animals, or things.
Use a **singular verb** when the group acts as **one unit**.
A **plural verb** may be used when the **members act separately**.

commonMistakes.urdu: کمیٹی منصوبے کی منظوری دیتی ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Committee acts as one unit here, so the singular verb approves is needed.

commonMistakes.wrong: The team are winning the match.
commonMistakes.right: The team is winning the match.
commonMistakes.urdu: ٹیم میچ جیت رہی ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Team is treated as one unit in this sentence, so use is.

commonMistakes.wrong: The jury have reached one decision.
commonMistakes.right: The jury has reached one decision.
commonMistakes.urdu: جیوری ایک فیصلے پر پہنچ چکی ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: One decision shows that the jury acts as a single unit, so use has.

practice.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The committee have agreed as one body.
The committee has agreed as one body.
practice.explanation: The committee acts as one unit, so has is correct.

practice.question: Which word is a collective noun?
practice.explanation: Flock names a group of birds.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: Committee acts as one unit.

quiz.question: Which is collective in “The army defended”?
quiz.explanation: Army names a group.

quiz.question: Choose the correct pronoun.
options: The jury announced their decision as one body.
The jury announced its decision as one body.
quiz.explanation: A single group takes its.

quiz.question: Which shows separate action?
options: The team are arguing among themselves.
quiz.explanation: Are shows members acting separately.

quiz.question: Choose the correct verb.
options: The flock of birds is moving south.
The flock of birds are moving souths.
The flock of birds moveing south.
The flock of birds be moving south.
quiz.explanation: Flock is the singular head noun.

ruleExamples: A **jury** reached one decision.
The **committee approves** the plan.
The **family are sitting** in different rooms.
types.exampleWords: family, team, jury, committee, staff

types.name: Abstract Noun
types.description: An Abstract Noun names an idea, quality, feeling, or state that cannot be touched.
types.urduExplanation: اسمِ کیفیت کسی خیال، خوبی، احساس یا حالت کا نام ہے جسے چھوا نہیں جا سکتا۔

examples.text: Honesty builds public trust.
examples.urdu: ایمان داری عوامی اعتماد پیدا کرتی ہے۔
examples.note: Honesty and trust are Abstract Nouns because they name qualities or ideas. Honesty is singular, so the verb is builds.

examples.text: Justice protects citizens.
examples.urdu: انصاف شہریوں کی حفاظت کرتا ہے۔
examples.note: Justice is an Abstract Noun naming an idea. It is singular, so it takes protects.

examples.text: The policy brought hope to families.
examples.urdu: پالیسی خاندانوں کے لیے امید لائی۔
examples.note: Hope is an Abstract Noun naming a feeling. It is the object of brought.

examples.text: Courage helps a candidate face difficulty.
examples.urdu: حوصلہ امیدوار کو مشکل کا سامنا کرنے میں مدد دیتا ہے۔
examples.note: Courage and difficulty are Abstract Nouns. Courage is the singular subject and takes helps.

rules: An **Abstract Noun** names an **idea, quality, feeling, or state**.
Abstract Nouns are often **uncountable** and take a **singular verb**.
Use an Abstract Noun to discuss an **idea or quality**, not a physical object.

commonMistakes.wrong: Honest is important in public service.
commonMistakes.right: Honesty is important in public service.
commonMistakes.urdu: عوامی خدمت میں ایمانداری اہم ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Honesty is the noun naming the quality; honest is an adjective.

commonMistakes.urdu: انصاف ضروری ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Justice is one Abstract Noun, so it takes is.

commonMistakes.urdu: پالیسی نے امید دی۔
commonMistakes.note: Hope is normally uncountable when it means a general feeling.

practice.question: Which is an abstract noun?
practice.explanation: Honesty names a quality that cannot be touched.

practice.question: Choose the noun formed from “brave”.
practice.explanation: Bravery is the standard abstract noun.

quiz.question: Which is abstract in “Justice should be equal”?
quiz.explanation: Justice names an idea.

quiz.question: Choose the correct verb.
quiz.explanation: Knowledge is singular and uncountable.

quiz.question: Which sentence has an abstract noun?
quiz.explanation: Courage names a quality.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form.
quiz.explanation: Advice is uncountable.

quiz.question: Which names a feeling?
quiz.explanation: Happiness names a feeling.

ruleExamples: **Honesty** is a valuable quality.
**Justice** is important in every court.
**Courage** helped the candidate face the interview.
types.exampleWords: honesty, courage, justice, freedom, wisdom

types.name: Countable Noun
types.description: A Countable Noun can be counted and has singular and plural forms.
types.urduExplanation: قابلِ شمار اسم کو گنا جا سکتا ہے اور اس کی واحد اور جمع شکلیں ہوتی ہیں۔

examples.text: One candidate submitted a form.
examples.urdu: ایک امیدوار نے فارم جمع کرایا۔
examples.note: Candidate and form are Countable Nouns. The singular subject one candidate takes submitted in the past tense.

examples.text: Three candidates passed the test.
examples.urdu: تین امیدوار امتحان میں کامیاب ہوئے۔
examples.note: Candidates is the plural form of the Countable Noun candidate. The plural subject takes passed in the past tense.

examples.text: The examiner checked two answers.
examples.urdu: ممتحن نے دو جوابات چیک کیے۔
examples.note: Answers is a plural Countable Noun because two answers can be counted.

examples.text: Several questions appeared in the paper.
examples.urdu: پرچے میں کئی سوالات آئے۔
examples.note: Questions is a plural Countable Noun. Several is used with a plural countable noun.

rules: A singular **Countable Noun** can take **a** or **an**.
Use **numbers** such as one, two, or several with Countable Nouns.
Plural Countable Nouns can take **many**, **few**, or **several**.

commonMistakes.urdu: اس نے دو کتابیں خریدیں۔
commonMistakes.note: A number greater than one needs the plural form books.

commonMistakes.urdu: وہاں بہت سے امیدوار ہیں۔
commonMistakes.note: Candidates is plural, so use are.

commonMistakes.urdu: میں نے ایک امیدوار دیکھا۔
commonMistakes.note: A singular noun takes a before the consonant sound in candidate.

practice.question: Which phrase is correct?
practice.explanation: University begins with a consonant sound, so a university is correct.

practice.question: Choose the correct plural form.
practice.explanation: Criteria is the plural of criterion in formal English.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: Books is plural and takes are.

quiz.question: Which fits “___ candidate passed”?
quiz.explanation: Candidate is singular with a vowel sound.

quiz.question: Choose the correct question.
quiz.explanation: Questions are plural countable nouns.

quiz.question: Which contains a countable noun?
quiz.explanation: Pens can be counted.

quiz.question: Choose the correct verb.
quiz.explanation: Students is plural.

ruleExamples: A **candidate** submitted a form.
Two **reports** reached the office.
Several **questions** appeared in the test.
types.exampleWords: book, candidate, question, report, document

types.name: Uncountable Noun
types.description: An Uncountable Noun names a substance, idea, or mass that is not counted separately.
types.urduExplanation: ناقابلِ شمار اسم ایسی چیز، مادے یا خیال کا نام ہے جسے الگ الگ نہیں گنا جاتا۔

examples.text: The research is useful for the examination.
examples.urdu: تحقیق امتحان کے لیے مفید ہے۔
examples.note: Research is an Uncountable Noun, so it takes the singular verb is. It is not normally written as researches for general research.

examples.text: The information was accurate.
examples.urdu: معلومات درست تھیں۔
examples.note: Information is Uncountable and takes the singular verb was. Do not write informations.

examples.text: The equipment is new.
examples.urdu: آلات نئے ہیں۔
examples.note: Equipment is Uncountable in English and takes is. Use pieces of equipment when counting items.

examples.text: The committee needs more evidence.
examples.urdu: کمیٹی کو مزید شواہد کی ضرورت ہے۔
examples.note: Evidence is Uncountable here, so more is used without a plural s.

rules: An **Uncountable Noun** names a substance, idea, or mass that is not normally counted separately.
Uncountable Nouns normally take a **singular verb**.
Use **much**, **little**, or **some**, not **a** or **an**, with many Uncountable Nouns.

commonMistakes.urdu: معلومات مفید ہیں۔
commonMistakes.note: Information is Uncountable in English, so it takes is.

commonMistakes.wrong: The researcher gave me many advices.
commonMistakes.right: The researcher gave me much advice.
commonMistakes.urdu: محقق نے مجھے بہت سے مشورے دیے۔
commonMistakes.note: Advice is Uncountable; use much advice or pieces of advice.

commonMistakes.urdu: لیبارٹری نے نئے آلات خریدے۔
commonMistakes.note: Equipment is Uncountable and does not normally take plural s.

practice.question: Choose the correct phrase.
practice.explanation: Information is uncountable and can be used with some.

practice.question: Which sentence is correct?
practice.explanation: Furniture is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: Information takes is.

quiz.question: Which phrase is correct?
quiz.explanation: A piece of advice is countable.

quiz.question: Choose the correct determiner.
quiz.explanation: Water is uncountable.

quiz.question: Which is uncountable in “The equipment is new”?
quiz.explanation: Equipment is uncountable.

quiz.question: Choose the correct verb.
quiz.explanation: Furniture takes is.

ruleExamples: **Information** is useful for candidates.
The **research** supports the policy.
The office needs **some equipment**.
types.exampleWords: water, advice, information, furniture, equipment

types.name: Material Noun
types.description: A Material Noun names a substance from which things are made.
types.urduExplanation: اسمِ مادہ اس چیز یا مادے کا نام ہے جس سے دوسری چیزیں بنائی جاتی ہیں۔

examples.text: The bridge is made of steel.
examples.urdu: پل فولاد سے بنا ہوا ہے۔
examples.note: Steel is a Material Noun naming the substance. Made of shows the material used; made by would name the maker.

examples.text: The table is made of wood.
examples.urdu: میز لکڑی سے بنی ہوئی ہے۔
examples.note: Wood is a Material Noun. Made of is correct because wood remains the material of the table.

examples.text: The officer wore a gold badge.
examples.urdu: افسر نے سونے کا بیج پہنا۔
examples.note: Gold is a Material Noun naming the substance used in the badge.

examples.text: The bottle is made from recycled plastic.
examples.urdu: بوتل ری سائیکل شدہ پلاسٹک سے بنی ہے۔
examples.note: Plastic is a Material Noun. Made from is used because the original material changes during production.

rules: A **Material Noun** names a **substance or material**.
Material Nouns are usually **uncountable** when they refer to material in general.
Use **made of** when the material is still easy to recognize.

commonMistakes.wrong: The chair is made for wood.
commonMistakes.right: The chair is made of wood.
commonMistakes.urdu: کرسی لکڑی سے بنی ہوئی ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Made of names the material; made for means purpose, not material.

commonMistakes.wrong: The bridge is made by steel.
commonMistakes.right: The bridge is made of steel.
commonMistakes.urdu: پل فولاد سے بنا ہوا ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Made by normally names the maker, while made of names the material.

commonMistakes.wrong: The badge is made with gold.
commonMistakes.right: The badge is made of gold.
commonMistakes.urdu: بیج سونے سے بنا ہوا ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Made of is the standard expression for the material of an object.

practice.question: Which is a material noun?
practice.explanation: Copper names a material.

practice.question: Choose the correct sentence.
practice.explanation: Water is normally uncountable and takes is.

quiz.question: Which is material in “The ring is silver”?
quiz.explanation: Silver names the material.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: Gold is uncountable.

quiz.question: Which is material in “The shirt is cotton”?
quiz.explanation: Cotton names the substance.

quiz.question: Choose the correct expression.
quiz.explanation: Use a unit to count steel.

quiz.question: Which uses a material noun correctly?
options: The chair is made of wood.
A wood is on the table.
quiz.explanation: Wood is an uncountable material.

ruleExamples: **Gold** is used in jewellery.
**Wood** is a useful material.
The chair is **made of wood**.
types.exampleWords: gold, wood, iron, cotton, silver

types.name: Compound Noun
types.description: A Compound Noun is made by joining two or more words to name one person, place, thing, or idea.
types.urduExplanation: مرکب اسم دو یا دو سے زیادہ الفاظ کو ملا کر ایک شخص، جگہ، چیز یا خیال کا نام بناتا ہے۔

examples.text: The examination hall opens at eight o’clock.
examples.urdu: امتحانی ہال آٹھ بجے کھلتا ہے۔
examples.note: Examination hall is a Compound Noun made from examination and hall. It names one place, so the singular verb opens is used.

examples.text: The research report is complete.
examples.urdu: تحقیقی رپورٹ مکمل ہے۔
examples.note: Research report is a Compound Noun made from research and report. It names one document.

examples.text: The policymaker announced a new plan.
examples.urdu: پالیسی ساز نے نیا منصوبہ سنایا۔
examples.note: Policymaker is a Compound Noun made from policy and maker. It names one person.

examples.text: The civil-service exam begins tomorrow.
examples.urdu: سول سروس کا امتحان کل شروع ہوتا ہے۔
examples.note: Civil-service exam is a Compound Noun phrase naming one examination.

rules: A **Compound Noun** joins **two or more words** to give one meaning.
Compound Nouns may be written as **one word, two words, or with a hyphen**.
In a compound noun, identify the **complete expression**, not only one word.

commonMistakes.urdu: امتحانی ہال جلد کھلتا ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: One hall is singular, so use hall and opens.

commonMistakes.urdu: پالیسی ساز منصوبہ بناتا ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Policymaker is one singular Compound Noun, so the verb is makes.

commonMistakes.wrong: The civil service exam are difficult.
commonMistakes.urdu: سول سروس کا امتحان مشکل ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: One exam is singular, so use is; the compound may be written with a hyphen.

practice.question: Which is a compound noun?
practice.explanation: Blackboard joins black and board to form one noun.

practice.question: Choose the correct plural.
practice.explanation: The main noun brother takes the plural form.

quiz.question: Choose the correct plural.
quiz.explanation: The main noun brother takes the plural.

quiz.question: Which is compound in “The classroom is bright”?
quiz.explanation: Classroom combines class and room.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: One bus stop is singular.

quiz.question: Correct plural of toothbrush?
quiz.explanation: Toothbrush takes -es.

quiz.question: Main noun in “mothers-in-law”?
quiz.explanation: Mother receives the plural ending.

ruleExamples: The **classroom** is ready for the lesson.
The **examination hall** opens at eight o’clock.
The **civil-service exam** begins tomorrow.
types.exampleWords: classroom, examination hall, policymaker, research report, civil-service exam

rules: A noun can work as the subject, object, complement, or object of a preposition.
Check capitalization, articles, plural forms, and verb agreement when identifying a noun in an exam sentence.
Some nouns change category according to meaning and context; do not memorize a label without reading the sentence.

examples.text: Ali is carrying a pen to school.
examples.urdu: علی ایک قلم لے کر اسکول جا رہا ہے۔
examples.note: Ali is a person, pen is a thing, and school is a place; all are Nouns.

commonMistakes.wrong: He gave me many useful advices.
commonMistakes.right: He gave me much useful advice.
commonMistakes.note: Advice is uncountable in standard English.

commonMistakes.wrong: The team are ready as one unit.
commonMistakes.right: The team is ready as one unit.
commonMistakes.note: Use a singular verb when a collective noun acts together.
Proper nouns and month names begin with capital letters.

examTips: In an error-detection question, first identify whether the noun is singular, plural, countable, or uncountable.
Remember irregular plurals and foreign plurals such as child/children, criterion/criteria, and phenomenon/phenomena.
For collective nouns, decide whether the group acts as one unit or as separate members before choosing the verb.

practice.question: Which word is a proper noun in “The delegation visited Lahore”?
practice.explanation: Lahore is the specific name of a city.

practice.question: Choose the correct sentence.
practice.explanation: Advice is uncountable and is used with some.

practice.question: Which is a material noun?
practice.explanation: Iron names a material.

quiz.question: What is the correct plural of “mother-in-law”?
quiz.explanation: The main noun mother takes the plural ending.

quiz.question: Which noun is abstract?
quiz.explanation: Freedom names an idea.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: Information is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

content.summary: Nouns name people, places, animals, things, materials, or ideas. For exam questions, identify the noun type, then check capitalization, articles, number, plural formation, possessive form, and subject–verb agreement. Context matters because one noun can have different classifications in different sentences.

content.introduction: A preposition is a word that shows the relationship between a noun or pronoun and another word in the sentence, often indicating place, time, direction, or manner.
content.urduExplanation: حرفِ جار وہ لفظ ہے جو کسی اسم یا اسمِ ضمیر کا جملے کے دوسرے الفاظ سے تعلق ظاہر کرتا ہے، جیسے جگہ، وقت، سمت یا طریقے کو بتانے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے۔
content.englishExplanation: Prepositions are essential for connecting ideas in a sentence. They typically precede a noun or pronoun (the object of the preposition) and show how that noun/pronoun relates to the rest of the sentence. Mastering prepositions is one of the most challenging aspects of English grammar for competitive exams because their usage often depends on fixed patterns and idioms rather than simple rules.

examples.text: in, on, at, by, with, for, from, to, into, between, among
examples.note: Common examples of prepositions.

types.name: Preposition of Time
types.description: A Preposition of Time allows you to discuss a specific time period such as a date on the calendar, one of the days of the week, or the actual time something takes place.
types.urduExplanation: حرفِ جارِ زمان وہ لفظ ہے جو وقت، تاریخ، دن یا کسی خاص مدت کو ظاہر کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے۔
types.exampleWords: at, on, in, since, for, during, until, by
rules: 1: Use **at** for precise times.
2: Use **on** for days and dates.
3: Use **in** for months, years, centuries, and long periods.
4: Use **since** to show a starting point in time.
5: Use **for** to show a duration or length of time.
6: Use **during** to show an action happening within a period.
ruleExamples:
I will meet you **at** 5 PM.
The train arrives **at** noon. > Precise time: **at**.

My birthday is **on** Monday.
We met **on** 15th August. > Days/Dates: **on**.

He was born **in** 1995.
It is cold **in** winter. > Months/Years/Seasons: **in**.

I have been here **since** morning.
She has lived here **since** 2010. > Starting point: **since**.

I waited **for** two hours.
They have been married **for** ten years. > Duration: **for**.

He fell asleep **during** the movie.
It rained **during** the night. > Within a period: **during**.

examples.text: I will meet you **at** 5 PM.
examples.urdu: میں آپ سے شام 5 بجے ملوں گا۔
examples.note: **At** is used for exact time.

examples.text: My birthday is **on** Monday.
examples.urdu: میری سالگرہ پیر کو ہے۔
examples.note: **On** is used for days of the week.

examples.text: He was born **in** 1995.
examples.urdu: وہ 1995 میں پیدا ہوا تھا۔
examples.note: **In** is used for years.

examples.text: I have been here **since** morning.
examples.urdu: میں صبح سے یہاں ہوں۔
examples.note: **Since** shows the starting point.

examples.text: I waited **for** two hours.
examples.urdu: میں نے دو گھنٹے انتظار کیا۔
examples.note: **For** shows the total duration.

commonMistakes.urdu: میں آپ سے 5 بجے ملوں گا۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **at** for specific clock times.

commonMistakes.urdu: میری سالگرہ پیر کو ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **on** for specific days.

commonMistakes.urdu: وہ 1995 میں پیدا ہوا تھا۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **in** for years.

commonMistakes.urdu: میں صبح سے یہاں ہوں۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **since** for a specific starting point.

commonMistakes.urdu: میں نے دو گھنٹے انتظار کیا۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **for** for a period of time.

types.name: Preposition of Place and Direction
types.description: These prepositions indicate where someone or something is located or the direction in which they are moving.
types.urduExplanation: حرفِ جارِ مکان و سمت وہ الفاظ ہیں جو کسی چیز کی جگہ، مقام یا حرکت کی سمت کو ظاہر کرتے ہیں۔
types.exampleWords: at, in, on, to, into, across, through, towards
rules: 1: Use **at** for a specific point or location.
2: Use **in** for an enclosed space or large area.
3: Use **on** for a surface.
4: Use **to** to show destination or direction.
5: Use **into** to show movement toward the inside of something.
6: Use **across** to show movement from one side to the other.
ruleExamples:
He is standing **at** the door.
Wait for me **at** the bus stop. > Specific point: **at**.

The keys are **in** the box.
He lives **in** London. > Enclosed space/Large area: **in**.

The book is **on** the table.
There is a picture **on** the wall. > Surface: **on**.

I am going **to** school.
He walked **to** the park. > Destination: **to**.

He jumped **into** the river.
She walked **into** the room. > Movement to inside: **into**.

They walked **across** the bridge.
He ran **across** the road. > Side to side: **across**.

examples.text: He is standing **at** the door.
examples.urdu: وہ دروازے پر کھڑا ہے۔
examples.note: **At** indicates a specific spot.

types.name: Preposition of Agency or Instrument
types.description: These prepositions show the relationship between the doer of an action and the action itself, or the tool used to perform an action.
types.urduExplanation: حرفِ جارِ ذریعہ یا آلہ وہ الفاظ ہیں جو کسی کام کے کرنے والے یا اس کام کے لیے استعمال ہونے والے آلے کے درمیان تعلق کو ظاہر کرتے ہیں۔
types.exampleWords: by, with, through, via
rules: 1: Use **by** for the person or agent who performs the action (usually in passive voice).
2: Use **with** for the instrument or tool used to perform the action.
3: Use **by** for means of transportation.
4: Use **through** to show the medium or process.
5: Use **via** to show the route or intermediate point.
ruleExamples:
The letter was written **by** Ali.
This book was published **by** a famous company. > Agent: **by**.

He wrote the letter **with** a pen.
She cut the apple **with** a knife. > Instrument: **with**.

I go to work **by** bus.
They traveled **by** air. > Transportation: **by**.

I learned the news **through** a friend.
Water flows **through** the pipe. > Medium: **through**.

We traveled to London **via** Dubai.
Send the file **via** email. > Route/Method: **via**.

examples.text: The letter was written **by** Ali.
examples.urdu: خط علی نے لکھا تھا۔

examples.text: He wrote the letter **with** a pen.

examples.note: **Via** shows the route.

commonMistakes.note: Use **by** for the person who does the work.

commonMistakes.note: Use **by** for general means of transport (without articles).

commonMistakes.note: Use **by** for the person performing the action.

types.name: Preposition of Possession
types.description: These prepositions indicate ownership or a relationship of belonging between two nouns.
types.urduExplanation: حرفِ جارِ ملکیت وہ الفاظ ہیں جو کسی چیز کی ملکیت یا دو چیزوں کے درمیان تعلق کو ظاہر کرتے ہیں۔
types.exampleWords: of, with, to
rules: 1: Use **of** to show belonging or connection (especially for non-living things).
2: Use **with** to show a feature or quality someone or something possesses.
3: Use **to** to show belonging to a person or group.
4: Use **of** for parts of a whole.
5: **Of** is often used in titles or descriptions.
ruleExamples:
The color **of** the car is red.
The legs **of** the table are broken. > Belonging (non-living): **of**.

The boy **with** blue eyes is my brother.
A girl **with** long hair. > Possession of a feature: **with**.

This book belongs **to** me.
He is a member **to** the club (often **of**). > Belonging to a person/group: **to**.

A piece **of** cake.
The handle **of** the door. > Part of a whole: **of**.

The King **of** Jordan.
The city **of** lights. > Titles/Descriptions: **of**.

examples.text: The color **of** the car is red.
examples.urdu: گاڑی کا رنگ سرخ ہے۔
examples.note: **Of** shows the relationship between color and car.

examples.note: **With** shows what he is carrying/wearing.

commonMistakes.note: Use possessive 's for people more often than **of**.

commonMistakes.note: Use **with** for physical features.

commonMistakes.note: The verb 'belong' always takes **to**.

commonMistakes.urdu: گھر کی چھت۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **of** for parts of non-living things.

commonMistakes.urdu: داڑھی والا آدمی۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **with** for physical attributes.

types.name: Preposition of Manner
types.description: These prepositions describe how an action is performed or the manner in which something happens.
types.urduExplanation: حرفِ جارِ طریقہ وہ الفاظ ہیں جو یہ بتاتے ہیں کہ کوئی کام کس طرح یا کس انداز سے کیا گیا۔
types.exampleWords: by, with, like, in
rules: 1: Use **by** to show the method or means of doing something.
2: Use **with** to show the feeling or attitude during an action.
3: Use **like** to show similarity or comparison.
4: Use **in** with certain phrases to show manner.
5: Use **with** to show the accompaniment of a quality.
ruleExamples:
He succeeded **by** working hard.
She escaped **by** jumping out. > Method: **by**.

He fought **with** courage.
She spoke **with** confidence. > Attitude/Feeling: **with**.

She sings **like** an angel.
He acts **like** a child. > Comparison: **like**.

He spoke **in** a loud voice.
They walked **in** silence. > Phrase-based manner: **in**.

He handled the situation **with** care.
She looked at him **with** anger. > Quality: **with**.

examples.text: He succeeded **by** working hard.

examples.note: **By** shows the method of success.

examples.text: He fought **with** courage.

examples.note: **With** shows the manner (courage).

examples.note: **Like** shows comparison.

commonMistakes.note: Use **by** for methods involving gerunds (-ing).

commonMistakes.note: Use **with** for abstract qualities like courage.

commonMistakes.note: Use **like** for comparison with a noun.

commonMistakes.note: The standard phrase is **in a ... voice**.

commonMistakes.note: Use **with** for care, precision, etc.

types.name: Compound Prepositions
types.description: Compound prepositions (also called Phrasal Prepositions) consist of two or more words that function as a single preposition.
types.urduExplanation: مرکب حروفِ جار وہ الفاظ ہیں جو دو یا دو سے زیادہ الفاظ پر مشتمل ہوتے ہیں لیکن ایک ہی حرفِ جار کے طور پر کام کرتے ہیں۔
types.exampleWords: in front of, instead of, because of, in spite of, according to
rules: 1: They function as a single unit to show relationships.
2: **Because of** shows a reason.
3: **Instead of** shows a substitution.
4: **In spite of** shows contrast or concession.
5: **According to** shows a source or standard.
ruleExamples:
He is sitting **in front of** the TV.
The car is parked **in front of** the house. > Position: **in front of**.

He was late **because of** the rain.
I am happy **because of** you. > Reason: **because of**.

Take tea **instead of** coffee.
He stayed home **instead of** going out. > Substitution: **instead of**.

He succeeded **in spite of** the difficulties.
They went out **in spite of** the rain. > Contrast: **in spite of**.

**According to** the news, it will rain.
Everything went **according to** plan. > Source/Standard: **according to**.

examples.urdu: وہ ٹی وی کے سامنے بیٹھا ہے۔

examples.note: **Instead of** shows substitution.

examples.note: **In spite of** shows contrast.

examples.urdu: سب کچھ منصوبے کے مطابق ہوا۔
examples.note: **According to** shows the standard.

commonMistakes.note: Don't forget the **to** in **according to**.

types.name: Participle Prepositions
types.description: These are verbs ending in -ing or -ed that function as prepositions in a sentence.
types.urduExplanation: فعلی حروفِ جار وہ الفاظ ہیں جو دراصل فعل کی صورتیں (ing یا ed والی) ہیں لیکن جملے میں حرفِ جار کے طور پر کام کرتے ہیں۔
types.exampleWords: concerning, regarding, including, following, considering
rules: 1: They act as connectors like other prepositions.
2: **Regarding** and **concerning** mean 'about'.
3: **Including** shows that something is part of a group.
4: **Following** means 'after'.
5: **Considering** means 'taking into account'.
ruleExamples:
I have a question **regarding** the project.
He wrote a letter **concerning** the issue. > About: **regarding/concerning**.

The price is $50, **including** tax.
Everyone came, **including** Ali. > Part of group: **including**.

**Following** the meeting, we had lunch.
He left **following** the argument. > After: **following**.

**Considering** his age, he is very active.
He did well, **considering** the circumstances. > Taking into account: **considering**.
I am **provided** with everything I need. (often functions as a participle preposition pattern).

examples.text: I have a question **regarding** the project.

examples.note: **Regarding** functions as a preposition meaning 'about'.

examples.note: **Considering** means taking his age into account.

commonMistakes.note: Use the participle form **regarding**.

commonMistakes.note: Use the participle form **including**.

commonMistakes.note: Use **concerning** meaning 'about'.

types.name: Preposition of Reason or Purpose
types.description: These prepositions indicate why an action is performed or the purpose behind it.
types.urduExplanation: حرفِ جارِ وجہ یا مقصد وہ الفاظ ہیں جو یہ بتاتے ہیں کہ کوئی کام کیوں کیا گیا یا اس کے پیچھے کیا مقصد تھا۔
types.exampleWords: for, of, from, because of, due to
rules: 1: Use **for** to show purpose or reason.
2: Use **of** to show the cause of death or illness.
3: Use **from** to show the source of a cause.
4: Use **because of** to introduce a reason (followed by a noun).
5: Use **due to** to show the cause (often following the verb 'to be').
ruleExamples:
I went there **for** a meeting.
She studies **for** knowledge. > Purpose: **for**.

He died **of** cancer.
She is sick **of** waiting. > Cause (illness/death): **of**.

He is suffering **from** fever.
She is tired **from** working. > Source of cause: **from**.

We stayed home **because of** the cold.
The flight was canceled **because of** fog. > Reason: **because of**.

The delay was **due to** heavy traffic.
His success is **due to** hard work. > Cause: **due to**.

examples.text: I went there **for** a meeting.

examples.note: **For** shows the purpose of going.

examples.note: **Because of** shows the reason.

examples.urdu: تاخیر ٹریفک کے رش کی وجہ سے تھی۔
examples.note: **Due to** shows the cause.

commonMistakes.note: Standard usage is **died of** for diseases.

commonMistakes.urdu: وہ بخار میں مبتلا ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: The verb 'suffer' takes the preposition **from**.

commonMistakes.urdu: میں میٹنگ کے لیے وہاں گیا۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **for** or **because of** before a noun.

commonMistakes.wrong: He is tired **of** working. (when you mean exhausted)
commonMistakes.urdu: وہ کام کرنے سے تھک گیا ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: **Tired of** means bored; **tired from** means exhausted.

commonMistakes.wrong: The match was canceled **due to** it rained.
commonMistakes.right: The match was canceled **because** it rained (or **due to** the rain).
commonMistakes.urdu: بارش کی وجہ سے میچ منسوخ ہو گیا۔
commonMistakes.note: **Due to** must be followed by a noun, not a clause.

types.name: Fixed Prepositions
types.description: Fixed prepositions, also called dependent prepositions, are prepositions conventionally required after particular verbs, adjectives, nouns, or expressions. This complete 120-expression reference groups common exam combinations by category. The preposition cannot normally be changed freely without changing standard usage or meaning.
types.urduExplanation: Fixed Prepositions، جنہیں Dependent Prepositions بھی کہا جاتا ہے، وہ حروفِ جار ہیں جو مخصوص افعال، صفات، اسماء یا تراکیب کے بعد مقررہ طور پر استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔ ان کے ساتھ دوسرا حرفِ جار لگانا عموماً غلط یا غیر فطری ہوتا ہے۔
types.exampleWords: 120 high-frequency expressions grouped as Verb + Preposition, Adjective + Preposition, Noun + Preposition, and Fixed Phrases/Zero-Preposition Traps.

examples.text: Good citizens **abide by** the law.
examples.urdu: اچھے شہری قانون کی پابندی کرتے ہیں۔
examples.note: **Abide** is followed by **by**, not with or on.

examples.text: The final result **depends on** accurate evidence.
examples.urdu: حتمی نتیجہ درست ثبوت پر منحصر ہوتا ہے۔
examples.note: **Depend on** means to rely on.

examples.text: The witness **insisted on** telling the truth.
examples.urdu: گواہ نے سچ بتانے پر اصرار کیا۔
examples.note: After a preposition, use a gerund: **insisted on telling**.

examples.text: The department **complied with** the court order.
examples.urdu: محکمے نے عدالتی حکم کی تعمیل کی۔
examples.note: **Comply with** means to act according to a rule or order.

examples.text: She is **capable of** handling difficult questions.
examples.urdu: وہ مشکل سوالات حل کرنے کی اہل ہے۔
examples.note: Use **of** after **capable**, followed by a noun or gerund.

examples.text: He is **responsible for** checking the documents.
examples.urdu: وہ دستاویزات کی جانچ کا ذمہ دار ہے۔
examples.note: Use **for**, not to, after **responsible** in this meaning.

examples.text: Every student should have **access to** reliable books.
examples.urdu: ہر طالب علم کو قابلِ اعتماد کتابوں تک رسائی ہونی چاہیے۔
examples.note: The noun **access** takes **to**.

examples.text: The committee found a **solution to** the problem.
examples.urdu: کمیٹی نے مسئلے کا حل تلاش کر لیا۔
examples.note: Use **to**, not of, after **solution**.

rules: Learn the complete combination rather than memorizing the word alone: depend on, not depend of.
A fixed preposition normally remains unchanged even when the tense or subject changes: depended on, is depending on.
When a verb is followed by a preposition, use a noun, pronoun, or gerund after it: insist on going.
Some adjectives require a particular preposition: afraid of, interested in, superior to, and responsible for.
Some nouns also take dependent prepositions: access to, demand for, reason for, and solution to.
Do not confuse fixed prepositions with freely chosen prepositions of time or place; fixed combinations must be learned as units.
ruleExamples: The answer depends on the context.
She insisted on speaking to the officer.
They objected to the proposed change.
He is interested in learning English.
The reason for the absence was recorded.
The committee searched for a solution to the dispute.

commonMistakes.urdu: کامیابی سخت محنت پر منحصر ہوتی ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **depend on**.

commonMistakes.urdu: اس نے اکیلے جانے پر اصرار کیا۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **insist on + gerund**, not insist to + verb.

commonMistakes.wrong: He is capable **to solve** the problem.
commonMistakes.right: He is capable **of solving** the problem.
commonMistakes.urdu: وہ مسئلہ حل کرنے کے قابل ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **capable of + gerund/noun**.

commonMistakes.urdu: وہ سائنس میں دلچسپی رکھتی ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: The correct combination is **interested in**.

commonMistakes.wrong: The officer is responsible **to** the project.
commonMistakes.right: The officer is responsible **for** the project.
commonMistakes.urdu: افسر منصوبے کا ذمہ دار ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **responsible for** when assigning responsibility.

commonMistakes.wrong: The students have access **of** the library.
commonMistakes.right: The students have access **to** the library.
commonMistakes.urdu: طلبہ کو کتب خانے تک رسائی حاصل ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: The noun **access** takes **to**.

commonMistakes.wrong: We need a solution **of** this problem.
commonMistakes.right: We need a solution **to** this problem.
commonMistakes.urdu: ہمیں اس مسئلے کا حل درکار ہے۔
commonMistakes.note: Use **solution to**.

commonMistakes.urdu: کمپنی نے ضابطے کی تعمیل کی۔
commonMistakes.note: The correct combination is **comply with**.
