title: Past Perfect Tense — ماضی مکمل
subtitle: Past Perfect Tense rules, formulas, and examples.

content.introduction:
1. Definition

Past Perfect Tense is used to describe an action that had been completed before another action or time in the past.


ماضی مکمل زمانہ ایسے کام کو ظاہر کرتا ہے جو ماضی میں کسی دوسرے کام یا وقت سے پہلے مکمل ہو چکا تھا۔
structure:
Affirmative — مثبت

Subject + had + V3 + Object

Ali had completed his work.
علی اپنا کام مکمل کر چکا تھا۔
Negative — منفی

Subject + had + not + V3 + Object

Ali had not completed his work.
علی نے اپنا کام مکمل نہیں کیا تھا۔
Interrogative — سوالیہ

Had + Subject + V3 + Object?

Had Ali completed his work?
کیا علی نے اپنا کام مکمل کر لیا تھا؟
rules:
1: Had with All Subjects

I, You, He, She, It, We, They, singular and plural nouns → had

Explanation: Had is used with all subjects, whether singular or plural
2: Always Use V3

The structure is:

had + V3

go → gone
write → written
eat → eaten
❌ He had went home.
✅ He had gone home.

Explanation: Had must be followed by the past participle (V3).
3:Two Past Actions

When two actions happened in the past, Past Perfect is generally used for the action that happened first, while Past Simple is used for the later action.

Ali had left before I arrived.
میرے پہنچنے سے پہلے علی جا چکا تھا۔

Explanation: Had left happened first; arrived happened later.
Before / After

Past Perfect is commonly used with before, after, when, by the time to show the order of past events.

She had left before I arrived.
میرے پہنچنے سے پہلے وہ جا چکی تھی۔
By the time we reached, the train had left.
جب تک ہم پہنچے، ٹرین جا چکی تھی۔

Explanation: These expressions help show which past action happened first.
example:
She had finished her work before dinner.
وہ کھانے سے پہلے اپنا کام مکمل کر چکی تھی۔
Explanation: The work was completed before another past time.
. They had reached the station when the train arrived.
جب ٹرین پہنچی تو وہ اسٹیشن پہنچ چکے تھے۔
Explanation: Their arrival happened before the train arrived.
They had not reached the station when the train arrived.
جب ٹرین پہنچی تو وہ اسٹیشن نہیں پہنچے تھے۔
Explanation: The action had not been completed before the other past action.

examples.text: Ali had completed his work.
examples.urdu: علی اپنا کام مکمل کر چکا تھا۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “Ali had completed his work.” — All subjects take “had”; the main verb in “Ali had completed his work.” must be the past participle V3.

examples.text: Ali had left before I arrived.
examples.urdu: میرے پہنچنے سے پہلے علی جا چکا تھا۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “Ali had left before I arrived.” — All subjects take “had”; the main verb in “Ali had left before I arrived.” must be the past participle V3.

examples.text: She had left before I arrived.
examples.urdu: میرے پہنچنے سے پہلے وہ جا چکی تھی۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “She had left before I arrived.” — All subjects take “had”; the main verb in “She had left before I arrived.” must be the past participle V3.

examples.text: By the time we reached, the train had left.
examples.urdu: جب تک ہم پہنچے، ٹرین جا چکی تھی۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “By the time we reached, the train had left.” — All subjects take “had”; the main verb in “By the time we reached, the train had left.” must be the past participle V3.

examples.text: They had finished the project before the deadline.
examples.urdu: انہوں نے مقررہ وقت سے پہلے منصوبہ مکمل کر لیا تھا۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “They had finished the project before the deadline.” — All subjects take “had”; the main verb in “They had finished the project before the deadline.” must be the past participle V3.

commonMistakes.urdu: وہ گھر جا چکا تھا۔
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “He had gone home.” — All subjects take “had”; the main verb in “He had gone home.” must be the past participle V3.

commonMistakes.urdu: وہ کام مکمل کر چکی تھی۔
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “She had finished the work.” — All subjects take “had”; the main verb in “She had finished the work.” must be the past participle V3.

commonMistakes.urdu: وہ مکمل کر چکے تھے۔
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “They had finished.” — All subjects take “had”; the main verb in “They had finished.” must be the past participle V3.

commonMistakes.urdu: کیا وہ اپنی خالہ سے مل چکی تھی؟
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “Had she visited her aunt?” — All subjects take “had”; the main verb in “Had she visited her aunt?” must be the past participle V3.

commonMistakes.urdu: وہ کھانا کھا چکا تھا۔
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “He had eaten dinner.” — All subjects take “had”; the main verb in “He had eaten dinner.” must be the past participle V3.

examTips: Affirmative → Subject + had + V3
Negative → Subject + had not + V3
Interrogative → Had + Subject + V3?
Key idea: Earlier past action → Past Perfect; later past action → Past Simple.

title: Past Continuous Tense — ماضی جاری
subtitle: Past Continuous Tense rules, formulas, and examples.

content.introduction:
1. Definition
Past Continuous Tense is used to describe an action that was in progress at a particular time in the past.

ماضی جاری زمانہ ایسے کام کو ظاہر کرتا ہے جو ماضی میں کسی خاص وقت جاری تھا۔
structure:
Affirmative — مثبت

Subject + was/were + V-ing + Object

Was → I, He, She, It, Singular noun
Were → You, We, They, Plural noun

He was reading a book.
وہ ایک کتاب پڑھ رہا تھا۔
They were playing cricket.
وہ کرکٹ کھیل رہے تھے۔

Negative — منفی

Subject + was/were + not + V-ing + Object

He was not reading a book.
وہ ایک کتاب نہیں پڑھ رہا تھا۔
They were not playing cricket.
وہ کرکٹ نہیں کھیل رہے تھے۔
Interrogative — سوالیہ

Was/Were + Subject + V-ing + Object?

Was he reading a book?
کیا وہ ایک کتاب پڑھ رہا تھا؟
Were they playing cricket?
کیا وہ کرکٹ کھیل رہے تھے؟
rules:
1: Was / Were

I, He, She, It, and singular nouns → was
You, We, They, and plural nouns → were
Explanation: Use was with singular subjects and were with plural subjects; you always takes were.

2: Use V-ing

The main verb always takes the -ing form.

He was reading.
They were playing.

Explanation: Past Continuous is formed with was/were + V-ing.
3: Interrupted Action

Past Continuous is often used for an action that was in progress when another past action occurred.

I was sleeping when the phone rang.
جب فون کی گھنٹی بجی تو میں سو رہا تھا۔

Explanation: Was sleeping was the ongoing action, while rang was the shorter action that interrupted it.
4: Two Actions in Progress

When two actions were happening at the same time in the past, Past Continuous can be used for both.

While I was studying, my brother was watching TV.
جب میں پڑھ رہا تھا، میرا بھائی ٹی وی دیکھ رہا تھا۔

Explanation: Both actions were in progress at the same time.

Example: 
They were playing cricket when it started to rain.
جب بارش شروع ہوئی تو وہ کرکٹ کھیل رہے تھے۔
Explanation: The ongoing action were playing was interrupted by another past action.
Ali was not studying at 8 p.m.
علی رات آٹھ بجے نہیں پڑھ رہا تھا۔
Explanation: “Ali” is singular, so we use was not + V-ing.
Were they playing cricket?
کیا وہ کرکٹ کھیل رہے تھے؟
Explanation: “They” is plural, so we use were before the subject.

examples.text: He was reading a book.
examples.urdu: وہ ایک کتاب پڑھ رہا تھا۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “He was reading a book.” — “He” takes “was”; the main verb uses -ing for an action in progress in the past.

examples.text: They were playing cricket.
examples.urdu: وہ کرکٹ کھیل رہے تھے۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “They were playing cricket.” — “They” takes “were”; the main verb uses -ing for an action in progress in the past.

examples.text: I was sleeping when the phone rang.
examples.urdu: جب فون کی گھنٹی بجی تو میں سو رہا تھا۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “I was sleeping when the phone rang.” — “I” takes “were”; the main verb uses -ing for an action in progress in the past.

examples.text: While I was studying, my brother was watching TV.
examples.urdu: جب میں پڑھ رہا تھا، میرا بھائی ٹی وی دیکھ رہا تھا۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “While I was studying, my brother was watching TV.” — “While” takes “was”; the main verb uses -ing for an action in progress in the past.

examples.text: They were playing cricket when it started to rain.
examples.urdu: جب بارش شروع ہوئی تو وہ کرکٹ کھیل رہے تھے۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “They were playing cricket when it started to rain.” — “They” takes “were”; the main verb uses -ing for an action in progress in the past.

commonMistakes.urdu: وہ کرکٹ کھیل رہے تھے۔
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “They were playing cricket.” — “They” takes “were”; the main verb uses -ing for an action in progress in the past.

commonMistakes.urdu: وہ پڑھ رہی تھی۔
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “She was studying.” — “She” takes “was”; the main verb uses -ing for an action in progress in the past.

commonMistakes.urdu: وہ کتاب پڑھ رہا تھا۔
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “He was reading a book.” — “He” takes “was”; the main verb uses -ing for an action in progress in the past.

commonMistakes.urdu: کیا وہ کام کر رہا تھا؟
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “Was he working?” — “Was” takes “was”; the main verb uses -ing for an action in progress in the past.

commonMistakes.urdu: میں سو رہا تھا۔
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “I was sleeping.” — “I” takes “were”; the main verb uses -ing for an action in progress in the past.

examTips: Affirmative → Subject + was/were + V-ing
Negative → Subject + was/were + not + V-ing
Interrogative → Was/Were + Subject + V-ing?

title: Past Indefinite Tense — ماضی سادہ
subtitle: Past Indefinite Tense rules, formulas, and examples.

content.introduction:
1. Definition

Past Indefinite Tense is used to describe an action that was completed at a definite or known time in the past.

ماضی سادہ زمانہ ایسے کام کو ظاہر کرتا ہے جو ماضی میں کسی وقت مکمل ہو چکا ہو۔
structure:
Affirmative مثبت

Subject + V2 + Object

He played cricket.
She visited Lahore.

Negative منفی

Subject + did not + V1 + Object

He did not play cricket.
She did not visit Lahore.

Interrogative سوالیہ

Did + Subject + V1 + Object?

Did he play cricket?
Did she visit Lahore?
rules:
1: Use V2 in Affirmative Sentences

In affirmative sentences, the main verb changes to its past form (V2).

go → went
play → played
write → wrote
2: Did + V1

After did or did not, always use V1.

❌ He did not went to school.
✅ He did not go to school.

Explanation: Did already shows the past tense, so the main verb remains in V1.
3: Same “did” for All Subjects

I, You, He, She, It, We, They, singular and plural nouns → did



Did he go? 

Did they go? 

 He did not go. 

 They did not go. 
Explanation: Did is used with all subjects in negative and interrogative sentences, whether singular or plural.

4: Common Past-Time Expressions

Past Indefinite is commonly used with:

yesterday, last night, last week, last year, ago, in 2020, once, when I was young

He visited Lahore last year.
She left two hours ago.
Explanation: These expressions indicate a completed action at a specific or finished time in the past, so we use the Past Indefinite Tense.
Example: Ali visited Lahore yesterday.
علی نے کل لاہور کا دورہ کیا۔
Explanation: The action was completed in the past, and “yesterday” shows a past time.
She passed the examination last year.
اس نے گزشتہ سال امتحان پاس کیا۔
Explanation: The action was completed at a specific time in the past.
Ali did not visit Lahore yesterday.
علی نے کل لاہور کا دورہ نہیں کیا۔
Explanation: “Ali” is singular, but after did not, we use the base verb visit (V1).
Did they play cricket yesterday?
کیا انہوں نے کل کرکٹ کھیلی؟
Explanation: After did, the main verb remains in its base form play (V1).

examples.text: Ali visited Lahore yesterday.
examples.urdu: علی نے کل لاہور کا دورہ کیا۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “Ali visited Lahore yesterday.” — “Ali” performs a completed past action, so the main verb in “Ali visited Lahore yesterday.” uses its correct V2 form.

examples.text: She passed the examination last year.
examples.urdu: اس نے گزشتہ سال امتحان پاس کیا۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “She passed the examination last year.” — “She” performs a completed past action, so the main verb in “She passed the examination last year.” uses its correct V2 form.

examples.text: Ali did not visit Lahore yesterday.
examples.urdu: علی نے کل لاہور کا دورہ نہیں کیا۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “Ali did not visit Lahore yesterday.” — After “did” or “did not”, the main verb in “Ali did not visit Lahore yesterday.” must stay in V1.

examples.text: Did they play cricket yesterday?
examples.urdu: کیا انہوں نے کل کرکٹ کھیلی؟
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “Did they play cricket yesterday?” — After “did” or “did not”, the main verb in “Did they play cricket yesterday?” must stay in V1.

examples.text: He went to school last week.
examples.urdu: وہ گزشتہ ہفتے اسکول گیا۔
examples.note: Explanation: Sentence “He went to school last week.” — “He” performs a completed past action, so the main verb in “He went to school last week.” uses its correct V2 form.

commonMistakes.wrong: He did not went to school.
commonMistakes.right: He did not go to school.
commonMistakes.urdu: وہ اسکول نہیں گیا۔
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “He did not go to school.” — After “did” or “did not”, the main verb in “He did not go to school.” must stay in V1.

commonMistakes.urdu: کیا وہ گھر گئی؟
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “Did she go home?” — After “did” or “did not”, the main verb in “Did she go home?” must stay in V1.

commonMistakes.urdu: وہ کل لاہور گیا۔
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “He went to Lahore yesterday.” — “He” performs a completed past action, so the main verb in “He went to Lahore yesterday.” uses its correct V2 form.

commonMistakes.urdu: انہوں نے کرکٹ نہیں کھیلی۔
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “They did not play cricket.” — After “did” or “did not”, the main verb in “They did not play cricket.” must stay in V1.

commonMistakes.urdu: کیا اس نے لاہور کا دورہ کیا؟
commonMistakes.note: Explanation: Correct form “Did he visit Lahore?” — After “did” or “did not”, the main verb in “Did he visit Lahore?” must stay in V1.

examTips: Affirmative → Subject + V2
Negative → Subject + did not + V1
Interrogative → Did + Subject + V1? [

title: Future Perfect Continuous Tense — مستقبل مکمل جاری
subtitle: Future Perfect Continuous Tense rules, formulas, and examples.

content.introduction:
1. Definition

Future Perfect Continuous Tense is used to describe an action that will have been continuing for a period of time up to a specific time in the future.

مستقبل مکمل جاری زمانہ ایسے کام کو ظاہر کرتا ہے جو مستقبل میں کسی خاص وقت تک ایک مخصوص مدت سے جاری ہوگا۔
structure:
Affirmative — مثبت

Subject + will have been + V-ing + Object

Ali will have been studying for three hours.
علی تین گھنٹے سے پڑھ رہا ہوگا۔
Negative — منفی

Subject + will not have been + V-ing + Object

Ali will not have been studying for three hours.
علی تین گھنٹے سے نہیں پڑھ رہا ہوگا۔
Interrogative — سوالیہ

Will + Subject + have been + V-ing + Object?

Will Ali have been studying for three hours?
کیا علی تین گھنٹے سے پڑھ رہا ہوگا؟
rules:
1: Will Have Been + V-ing

All subjects → will have been + V-ing

Explanation: Future Perfect Continuous uses will have been + V-ing with all subjects.
2: Always Use V-ing
study → studying
work → working
play → playing

❌ He will have been study.
✅ He will have been studying.

Explanation: The main verb must be in the -ing form.
3: Since and For

Since → the starting point of an action
اردو: کسی کام کے شروع ہونے کا وقت

For → the duration of an action
اردو: کسی کام کے جاری رہنے کا دورانیہ

He will have been studying since morning.
وہ صبح سے پڑھ رہا ہوگا۔
He will have been studying for three hours.
وہ تین گھنٹے سے پڑھ رہا ہوگا۔

Explanation: Since tells when the action started, while for tells how long it has continued.
4: Duration Up to a Future Time

Use Future Perfect Continuous when an action will continue for a period of time up to a specific future time or event.

She will have been waiting for two hours by 6 p.m.
وہ شام چھ بجے تک دو گھنٹے سے انتظار کر رہی ہوگی۔

Explanation: The sentence focuses on the duration of the ongoing action up to a future point.
Common Time Expressions

for two hours, for five years, since morning, since Monday, by tomorrow, by next year, by the time

By next year, he will have been teaching for ten years.
اگلے سال تک اسے پڑھاتے ہوئے دس سال ہو چکے ہوں گے۔

Explanation: “For ten years” shows the duration, while “by next year” gives the future point.
Ali will have been studying for three hours by 8 p.m.
علی رات آٹھ بجے تک تین گھنٹے سے پڑھ رہا ہوگا۔
Explanation: The action will continue for three hours up to a specific future time.
She will have been waiting for an hour by the time the bus arrives.
جب بس پہنچے گی تو اسے انتظار کرتے ہوئے ایک گھنٹہ ہو چکا ہوگا۔
Explanation: The waiting will continue for one hour before the future event.
They will not have been working here for five years by next month.

title: Future Perfect Tense — مستقبل مکمل
subtitle: Future Perfect Tense rules, formulas, and examples.

content.introduction:
1. Definition

Future Perfect Tense is used to describe an action that will have been completed before a specific time or another action in the future.
مستقبل مکمل زمانہ ایسے کام کو ظاہر کرتا ہے جو مستقبل میں کسی خاص وقت یا دوسرے کام سے پہلے مکمل ہو چکا ہوگا۔
structure:
Affirmative — مثبت

Subject + will have + V3 + Object

Ali will have completed his work.
علی اپنا کام مکمل کر چکا ہوگا۔
Negative — منفی

Subject + will not have + V3 + Object

Ali will not have completed his work.
علی اپنا کام مکمل نہیں کر چکا ہوگا۔
Interrogative — سوالیہ

Will + Subject + have + V3 + Object?

Will Ali have completed his work?
کیا علی اپنا کام مکمل کر چکا ہوگا؟
rules:
1: Will Have + V3

All subjects → will have + V3

Explanation: Future Perfect uses will have + V3 with all subjects. [Certain]

He will have finished.
They will have finished.
2:Always Use V3
go → gone
write → written
complete → completed

❌ He will have went home.
✅ He will have gone home.

Explanation: The verb after will have must be in its V3 form.
3: By + Future Time

Future Perfect is commonly used with by to show the deadline or future point before which an action will be completed.

She will have finished the work by Monday.
وہ پیر تک کام مکمل کر چکی ہوگی۔

Explanation: “By Monday” means the action will be completed on or before Monday.
4: Before Another Future Action

They will have left before we arrive.
ہمارے پہنچنے سے پہلے وہ جا چکے ہوں گے۔

Explanation: Will have left shows the action that will be completed first.
5: Common Time Expressions

by tomorrow, by next week, by next year, by 8 p.m., before, by the time

He will have returned by next week.
وہ اگلے ہفتے تک واپس آ چکا ہوگا۔

Explanation: These expressions indicate the future point by which the action will be completed.
Example:
Ali will have completed his assignment by tomorrow.
علی کل تک اپنا اسائنمنٹ مکمل کر چکا ہوگا۔
Explanation: The action will be completed before a specific future time, “tomorrow.”
. They will have finished the project before the deadline.
وہ مقررہ وقت سے پہلے منصوبہ مکمل کر چکے ہوں گے۔
Explanation: The project will be completed before another future point.
They will not have finished the project by Friday.
وہ جمعہ تک منصوبہ مکمل نہیں کر چکے ہوں گے۔
Explanation: The completion will not have happened by Friday.
Will Ali have completed his assignment by tomorrow?
کیا علی کل تک اپنا اسائنمنٹ مکمل کر چکا ہوگا؟
Explanation: Will comes before the subject, followed by have + V3.

title: Future Continuous Tense — مستقبل جاری
subtitle: Future Continuous Tense rules, formulas, and examples.

content.introduction:
1. Definition

Future Continuous Tense is used to describe an action that will be in progress at a particular time in the future.

مستقبل جاری زمانہ ایسے کام کو ظاہر کرتا ہے جو مستقبل میں کسی خاص وقت جاری ہوگا۔
structure:
Affirmative — مثبت

Subject + will be + V-ing + Object

I will be studying English.
میں انگریزی پڑھ رہا ہوں گا۔
Negative — منفی

Subject + will not be + V-ing + Object

They will not be playing cricket.
وہ کرکٹ نہیں کھیل رہے ہوں گے۔

Interrogative — سوالیہ

Will + Subject + be + V-ing + Object?

Will you be studying English?
کیا آپ انگریزی پڑھ رہے ہوں گے؟
rules:
Rule 1 — Will Be + V-ing

All subjects → will be + V-ing

Explanation: Future Continuous uses will be + V-ing with all subjects.
Specific Future Time

Future Continuous commonly describes an action that will be in progress at a particular time in the future.

At 10 p.m. tonight, I will be studying.
آج رات دس بجے میں پڑھ رہا ہوں گا۔

Explanation: “At 10 p.m. tonight” specifies the future time when the action will be in progress.
Example:
Ali will be studying at 8 p.m.
علی رات آٹھ بجے پڑھ رہا ہوگا۔
Explanation: The action will be in progress at a specific time in the future.
She will be preparing for the exam next week.
وہ اگلے ہفتے امتحان کی تیاری کر رہی ہوگی۔
Explanation: The action will be in progress during a future period.
They will not be travelling tomorrow morning.
وہ کل صبح سفر نہیں کر رہے ہوں گے۔
Explanation: The action will not be in progress at that future time.
Will Ali be studying at 8 p.m.?
کیا علی رات آٹھ بجے پڑھ رہا ہوگا؟
Explanation: Will comes before the subject, followed by be + V-ing.

title: Future Indefinite Tense — مستقبل سادہ
subtitle: Future Indefinite Tense rules, formulas, and examples.

content.introduction:
1. Definition

Future Indefinite Tense is used to describe an action that will happen or take place in the future.

مستقبل سادہ زمانہ ایسے کام کو ظاہر کرتا ہے جو آنے والے وقت میں ہوگا یا کیا جائے گا۔
structure:
Affirmative — مثبت

Subject + will + V1 + Object

I will study English.
میں انگریزی پڑھوں گا۔
They will play cricket.
وہ کرکٹ کھیلیں گے۔
Negative — منفی

Subject + will not + V1 + Object

I will not study English.
میں انگریزی نہیں پڑھوں گا۔
They will not play cricket.
وہ کرکٹ نہیں کھیلیں گے۔
Interrogative — سوالیہ

Will + Subject + V1 + Object?

Will you study English?
کیا آپ انگریزی پڑھیں گے؟
Will they play cricket?
کیا وہ کرکٹ کھیلیں گے؟
rules:
1: Will + V1

Use will + V1 for all subjects.

I, You, He, She, It, We, They → will + V1

Explanation: Will is used with all subjects, and the main verb remains in its base form (V1).

Future Time Expressions

Common expressions include:

tomorrow, next week, next month, next year, soon, later, in the future

She will arrive tomorrow.
We will meet next week.

Explanation: These expressions commonly indicate future time.
Example: 
Ali will visit Lahore next week.
علی اگلے ہفتے لاہور جائے گا۔
Explanation: The action is expected to happen in the future, so we use will + V1.
They will complete the project soon.
وہ جلد ہی منصوبہ مکمل کریں گے۔
Explanation: The action will take place in the future.
Ali will not visit Lahore next week.
علی اگلے ہفتے لاہور نہیں جائے گا۔
Explanation: Will not makes the future action negative.
Will they attend the meeting?
کیا وہ اجلاس میں شرکت کریں گے؟
Explanation: The question is formed with will + subject + V1.

title: Phrases
subtitle: 8 phrase types and how to spot them
summary: A complete exam-oriented guide to phrase structure, functions, identification, examples, and common errors.

content.providedMaterial:
Independent Clause
Definition

English:
An independent clause is a group of words that contains a subject and a verb and expresses a complete thought.

Urdu:
Independent Clause (مکمل جملے کا جز) الفاظ کا ایسا مجموعہ ہے جس میں Subject اور Verb ہوتے ہیں اور جو مکمل خیال بیان کرتا ہے۔

Examples
She is studying for the exam.
Ali plays football every evening.
We went to the market yesterday.

In each example, the clause has a subject and a verb and gives a complete meaning.

Structure

Subject + Verb + Complete Idea

Examples:

She + is studying + for the exam.
Ali + plays + football every evening.
We + went + to the market yesterday.
Main Function

An independent clause can stand alone as a complete sentence.

Example:

The students completed their work.

This is an independent clause because it has:

Subject: The students
Verb: completed
Complete thought: The students completed their work.
How to Identify an Independent Clause

Ask these two questions:

Does it have a subject and a verb?
Does it express a complete thought?

If the answer to both is yes, it is an Independent Clause.

Compare

Independent Clause:

She went home. ✓

It gives a complete thought.

Not Independent:

Because she was tired ✗

It has a subject (she) and verb (was), but it does not give a complete thought by itself.

Easy Rule

Independent Clause = Subject + Verb + Complete Thought

Exam Tip

If a clause can stand alone as a complete sentence, it is an Independent Clause.

Dependent Clause
Definition

English:
A dependent clause is a group of words that contains a subject and a verb but does not express a complete thought by itself.

Urdu:
Dependent Clause (نامکمل جملے کا جز) الفاظ کا ایسا مجموعہ ہے جس میں Subject اور Verb ہوتے ہیں، لیکن یہ اکیلا مکمل خیال بیان نہیں کرتا۔

Examples
because she was tired, she went home.
I will call you when I reach home.
Although he studied hard, he failed the exam.

In each example, the bold words have a subject and a verb but cannot stand alone as a complete sentence.

Structure

Subordinating Word + Subject + Verb + Incomplete Idea

Examples:

because + she + was tired
when + I + reach home
although + he + studied hard
Main Function

A dependent clause cannot stand alone. It must be connected to an independent clause to form a complete sentence.

Example:

Because she was tired, she went home.

Dependent Clause: Because she was tired
Independent Clause: she went home

The dependent clause explains why she went home.

How to Identify a Dependent Clause

Ask these two questions:

Does it have a subject and a verb?
Can it stand alone as a complete sentence?

If it has a subject and verb but cannot stand alone, it is a Dependent Clause.

Compare

Independent Clause:

She went home. ✓

Complete thought.

Dependent Clause:

Because she was tired. ✗

It leaves the reader asking: What happened because she was tired?

Common Words That Introduce Dependent Clauses
because
although
if
when
while
before
after
unless
since
that
who
which
Easy Rule

Dependent Clause = Subject + Verb + Incomplete Thought

Exam Tip

If a group of words has a subject and verb but cannot stand alone, it is a Dependent Clause.

Noun Clause
Definition

English:
A noun clause is a group of words that contains a subject and a verb and works like a noun in a sentence.

Urdu:
Noun Clause (اسمی جملے کا جز) الفاظ کا ایسا مجموعہ ہے جس میں Subject اور Verb ہوتے ہیں اور جو جملے میں Noun (اسم) کی طرح کام کرتا ہے۔

Examples

I know that he is honest.
میں جانتا ہوں کہ وہ ایماندار ہے۔

What she said was true.
اس نے جو کہا وہ سچ تھا۔

She explained why she was late.
اس نے وضاحت کی کہ وہ دیر سے کیوں آئی۔

In each example, the bold words contain a subject and a verb and work like a noun.

Common Structure

Subject + Verb + Noun Clause

Examples:

I know that he is honest.
She explained why she was late.
We don't know where he lives.

A noun clause can begin with words such as:

that, what, who, why, where, when, how, whether, if

Functions of a Noun Clause

A noun clause can work as:

Function	Example
Subject	What he said was true.
Object	I know that she is honest.
Subject Complement	The problem is that we are late.
Object of a Preposition	We talked about what he had done.
How to Identify a Noun Clause

Look for a group of words that:

Contains a subject and a verb.
Cannot normally stand alone as a complete sentence.
Works like a noun in the main sentence.

Example:

I don't know where he lives.

Noun Clause: where he lives
Subject: he
Verb: lives
Function: Object of know
How a Noun Clause Adds Information

A noun clause can replace a simple noun and express a complete idea as a thing, fact, question, or information.

Simple:

I know the answer.

More information:

I know what the answer is.

Here:

the answer → noun
what the answer is → noun clause
Both work as the object of know.
Easy Rule

Noun Clause = Subject + Verb + works like a Noun

Exam Tip

Ask: “Is this clause doing the job of a noun?” If yes, it is a Noun Clause.

Adjective Clause
Definition

English:
An adjective clause is a group of words that contains a subject and a verb and describes or gives more information about a noun or pronoun.

Urdu:
Adjective Clause (صفتی جملے کا جز) الفاظ کا ایسا مجموعہ ہے جس میں Subject اور Verb ہوتے ہیں اور جو کسی Noun یا Pronoun کے بارے میں مزید معلومات دیتا ہے۔

Examples

The boy who won the race is my brother.
وہ لڑکا جس نے دوڑ جیتی میرا بھائی ہے۔

I met a woman who works at the hospital.
میں ایک ایسی عورت سے ملا جو ہسپتال میں کام کرتی ہے۔

This is the book that I bought yesterday.
یہ وہ کتاب ہے جو میں نے کل خریدی تھی۔

In each example, the bold clause describes or identifies a noun.

Common Structure

Noun + Relative Word + Subject + Verb

Examples:

the boy who won the race
the woman who works at the hospital
the book that I bought yesterday

Common words used to introduce adjective clauses:

who, whom, whose, which, that, where, when

Function of an Adjective Clause

An adjective clause mainly describes or identifies a noun or pronoun.

Function	Example
Describe a person	The girl who is wearing a red dress is my sister.
Describe a thing	I read the book that you recommended.
Identify a place	This is the school where I studied.
Identify a time	I remember the day when we first met.
How to Identify an Adjective Clause

Look for a group of words that:

Contains a subject and a verb.
Gives information about a noun or pronoun.
Usually begins with a relative word such as who, which, that, whose, where, or when.

Example:

The student who studies regularly gets good marks.

Adjective Clause: who studies regularly
Subject: who
Verb: studies
Describes: student
Function: Gives more information about the noun student.
How an Adjective Clause Adds Information

An adjective clause makes a noun more specific by telling us which person or thing we mean.

Simple:

I met a girl.

More information:

I met a girl who won the competition.

Here:

girl → main noun
who won the competition → describes the girl
The clause tells us which girl.
Easy Rule

Adjective Clause = Subject + Verb + describes a Noun or Pronoun

Exam Tip

Ask: “Which noun or pronoun does this clause describe?” If it describes a noun or pronoun, it is an Adjective Clause.

Adverb Clause
Definition

English:
An adverb clause is a group of words that contains a subject and a verb and gives more information about a verb, adjective, or the whole main clause.

Urdu:
Adverb Clause (حالیہ جملے کا جز) الفاظ کا ایسا مجموعہ ہے جس میں Subject اور Verb ہوتے ہیں اور جو جملے میں وقت، وجہ، شرط، مقصد، نتیجہ یا تضاد جیسی معلومات دیتا ہے۔

Examples

We stayed inside because it was raining.
ہم اندر رہے کیونکہ بارش ہو رہی تھی۔

When the teacher arrived, the students became quiet.
جب استاد آئے، طلبہ خاموش ہو گئے۔

I will help you if you need me.
میں آپ کی مدد کروں گا اگر آپ کو میری ضرورت ہو۔

In each example, the bold clause gives additional information about the main action.

Common Structure

Subordinating Conjunction + Subject + Verb

Examples:

because + it was raining
when + the teacher arrived
if + you need me

Common words that introduce adverb clauses:

because, when, while, before, after, if, unless, although, since, as, so that

Functions of an Adverb Clause

An adverb clause can show:

Function	Example
Time	I will call you when I reach home.
Reason	We stayed inside because it was raining.
Condition	I will help you if you need me.
Contrast	Although he was tired, he continued working.
Purpose	She studies hard so that she can pass the exam.
How to Identify an Adverb Clause

Look for a group of words that:

Contains a subject and a verb.
Cannot normally stand alone as a complete sentence.
Gives information about the main action or situation.
Often answers when, why, under what condition, or despite what.

Example:

We stayed home because it was raining.

Adverb Clause: because it was raining
Subject: it
Verb: was raining
Function: Shows reason
Describes: Why we stayed home
How an Adverb Clause Adds Information

An adverb clause gives additional information about when, why, how, or under what condition something happens.

Simple:

We stayed home.

More information:

We stayed home because it was raining.

Here:

We stayed home → main clause
because it was raining → tells why we stayed home

Another example:

Simple:

I will call you.

More information:

I will call you when I reach home.

Here:

I will call you → main clause
when I reach home → tells when I will call
Easy Rule

Adverb Clause = Subject + Verb + gives information about the main action or situation.

Exam Tip

Ask “When? Why? Under what condition? or Despite what?” If the clause answers one of these questions about the main clause, it is likely an Adverb Clause.

Phrase vs Clause
Basic Difference

A phrase does not normally contain a complete subject–verb combination, while a clause contains a subject and a verb.

| Phrase                                                 | Clause                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Does not normally contain a subject + verb combination | Contains a subject + verb                                  |
| Does not express a complete thought by itself          | May express a complete thought or depend on another clause |
| Works as a part of a sentence                          | Can form part or all of a sentence                         |
| **in the morning**                                     | **when the morning came**                                  |
| **after the class**                                    | **after the class ended**                                  |
| **the intelligent student**                            | **the student who studies hard**                           |


Examples

Phrase:

We met after the class.

after the class → Phrase
No subject + verb combination

Clause:

We met after the class ended.

after the class ended → Clause
the class → Subject
ended → Verb
Easy Rule

Phrase → No complete Subject + Verb
Clause → Subject + Verb

Exam Tip

When you see a group of words in an exam, first look for the subject and verb. [Certain]

No subject + verb → likely a Phrase
Subject + verb → Clause

title: Subject–Verb Agreement
subtitle: The verb must match its subject in number and person, even when other words s...

content.englishExplanation:
Subject-verb agreement means the verb form must match the number (singular or plural) and person (first, second, third) of its subject. This is straightforward in most sentences, but becomes tricky when phrases, clauses, or special noun types intervene between subject and verb.

Key trouble spots include collective nouns (team, committee), indefinite pronouns (everyone, each, neither), compound subjects joined by 'or/nor', and subjects that look plural but are grammatically singular (e.g., news, mathematics).
rules: A singular subject takes a singular verb; a plural subject takes a plural verb.
Phrases between the subject and verb do not change the subject's number.
Compound subjects joined by 'and' normally take a plural verb.
When subjects are joined by 'or' or 'nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
Indefinite pronouns like everyone, each, and neither take a singular verb.
Collective nouns (team, jury, family) take a singular verb when acting as a unit, plural when individual members are emphasised.
Nouns that end in -s but refer to a single item (news, mathematics, economics) take a singular verb.

examples.text: The box of chocolates is on the table.
examples.note: subject is 'box', not 'chocolates'

examples.text: Neither the students nor the teacher knows the answer.
examples.note: 'nor' rule: verb agrees with 'teacher' (nearer)

examples.text: Everyone is invited to the party.
examples.note: 'Everyone' is singular

examples.text: The committee has made its decision.
examples.note: collective noun as unit: singular verb

examples.text: Mathematics is my favourite subject.
examples.note: singular despite ending in -s

commonMistakes.wrong: The team are playing well today.
commonMistakes.right: The team is playing well today.
commonMistakes.note: in American English, collective nouns take singular verbs when acting as a unit

commonMistakes.wrong: Each of the students have a book.
commonMistakes.right: Each of the students has a book.
commonMistakes.note: 'each' is singular

commonMistakes.wrong: Either the manager or the employees is responsible.
commonMistakes.right: Either the manager or the employees are responsible.
commonMistakes.note: verb agrees with the nearer subject 'employees'

commonMistakes.wrong: There was many people at the event.
commonMistakes.right: There were many people at the event.
commonMistakes.note: verb agrees with the real subject 'people', which is plural

practice.question: Choose the correct verb: 'The quality of her essays ___ improved greatly.'
practice.explanation: The subject is 'quality' (singular), not 'essays'; the verb 'has' is correct.

practice.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Neither he nor she are ready.
Neither he nor she is ready.
Neither he nor she were ready.
Neither he nor she am ready.
practice.explanation: With 'nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'she' (third person singular), so 'is' is correct.

practice.question: Select the correct form: 'News ___ fast in a connected world.'
practice.explanation: 'News' ends in -s but is a singular noun, requiring the singular verb 'travels'.

practice.question: Which indefinite pronoun always takes a singular verb?
practice.explanation: 'Each' is always singular: 'Each of the players has a role.'

title: Common Errors
subtitle: Frequent grammar mistakes including confusing homophones, dangling modifiers,...

content.englishExplanation:
Even proficient writers make recurring mistakes. The most common fall into several categories: confusing look-alike or sound-alike words (affect/effect, their/there/they're), incorrect pronoun case, dangling or misplaced modifiers, double negatives, subject-verb disagreement, comma splices, and sentence fragments.

Recognising these patterns and learning systematic ways to check for them is more effective than simply memorising rules. Many errors can be caught by reading work aloud, looking for specific trigger words, or applying a targeted revision checklist.
rules: Affect is usually a verb; effect is usually a noun.
Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they) for sentence subjects; use object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them) elsewhere.
Avoid double negatives: 'I don't know anything' (not 'I don't know nothing').
Place modifying words or phrases as close as possible to the word they modify.
A comma splice occurs when two independent clauses are joined with only a comma; fix it with a conjunction, semicolon, or period.
Fewer is used with countable nouns; less with uncountable nouns.
Who refers to people; that or which refer to things.

examples.text: The new law will affect everyone.
examples.note: 'affect' = verb

examples.text: The effect of the new law is significant.
examples.note: 'effect' = noun

examples.text: Between you and me, I prefer tea.
examples.note: object pronoun 'me' after preposition

examples.text: Only she knows the answer.
examples.note: 'only' placed correctly before the word it modifies

examples.text: There were fewer students this year.
examples.note: 'fewer' for countable noun 'students'

commonMistakes.note: double negative: one negative per clause

commonMistakes.wrong: Between you and I, it is wrong.
commonMistakes.right: Between you and me, it is wrong.
commonMistakes.note: preposition 'between' requires object pronoun 'me'

commonMistakes.wrong: There is less people here today.
commonMistakes.right: There are fewer people here today.
commonMistakes.note: plural subject 'people' needs plural verb; 'fewer' for countable nouns

commonMistakes.wrong: The manager which called is new.
commonMistakes.right: The manager who called is new.
commonMistakes.note: use 'who' for people, not 'which'

commonMistakes.wrong: She past the exam with high marks.
commonMistakes.right: She passed the exam with high marks.
commonMistakes.note: 'passed' is the verb; 'past' is an adjective/preposition/noun

practice.question: Which sentence uses 'affect' and 'effect' correctly?
options: The effect of the storm affected.
The affect of the storm was huge.
practice.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to influence; 'the storm affected our plans' is correct.

practice.question: Identify the error: 'Me and my friend went to the cinema.'
options: 'Me' should be 'I' as a sentence subject.
practice.explanation: Subject pronouns are required for sentence subjects; 'I and my friend' or 'My friend and I' is correct.

practice.question: Which sentence avoids a double negative?
practice.explanation: 'He didn't do anything wrong' uses one negative element; the others all use two, creating a double negative.

practice.question: Choose the sentence with correct pronoun use:
practice.explanation: After the linking verb 'was', a subject complement is required; 'she' (subject form) is correct.

content.providedMaterial:
Adjective Phrase
Definition

English:
An adjective phrase is a group of words that works like an adjective and gives more information about a noun or pronoun.

Urdu:
ایسے الفاظ کے مجموعے کو صفتی فقرہ (Adjective Phrase) کہتے ہیں جو اسم (Noun) یا ضمیر (Pronoun) کے بارے میں مزید معلومات فراہم کرے۔

Examples

The girl with long hair is my sister.
لمبے بالوں والی لڑکی میری بہن ہے۔

He is a man full of courage.
وہ ہمت سے بھرپور آدمی ہے۔

I bought a dress very suitable for the party.
میں نے ایک ایسا لباس خریدا جو پارٹی کے لیے بہت موزوں ہے۔

In each example, the bold words describe or give more information about a noun.

Common Structure

Adjective + Modifier(s)

Examples:

very beautiful
extremely intelligent
full of confidence
rich in experience

Note: An adjective phrase does not always follow only the Adjective + Modifier pattern. It can contain other words that work together to describe a noun.

Examples:

full of hope
very proud of his son
extremely useful for students
Functions of an Adjective Phrase

An adjective phrase can:

Example
The girl with long hair is my sister.
Someone very close to me called today.
We visited a place rich in history.
She is very happy with her results.
How to Identify an Adjective Phrase

Look for a group of words that describes or gives more information about a noun or pronoun.

Example:

The man with a long beard is my uncle.

Adjective Phrase: with a long beard
Describes: man
Function: Gives more information about the noun man
How an Adjective Phrase Adds Information

An adjective phrase makes a noun more specific by describing its quality, appearance, condition, or other characteristics.

Simple:

I saw a man.

More information:

I saw a man with a long beard.

Here:

man → main noun
with a long beard → describes the man
The adjective phrase makes the noun more specific.

Another example:

Simple:

She lives in a house.

More information:

She lives in a house full of beautiful paintings.

Here:

house → main noun
full of beautiful paintings → describes the house
The phrase gives more information about the house.
Easy Rule

An adjective phrase describes or gives more information about a noun or pronoun.

Exam Tip

Ask: “Which noun or pronoun does this group of words describe?” If it describes a noun or pronoun, it

Adverb Phrase
Definition

English:
An adverb phrase is a group of words that works like an adverb and gives more information about a verb, adjective, or another adverb.

Urdu:
ایسے الفاظ کے مجموعے کو حالی فقرہ (Adverb Phrase) کہتے ہیں جو فعل (Verb)، صفت (Adjective) یا دوسرے حال (Adverb) کے بارے میں مزید معلومات فراہم کرے۔

Examples

He speaks with great confidence.
وہ بہت اعتماد کے ساتھ بات کرتا ہے۔

She arrived very early in the morning.
وہ صبح بہت سویرے پہنچی۔

They worked with great care.
انہوں نے بہت احتیاط سے کام کیا۔

In each example, the bold words give more information about the action.

Common Structure

Adverb + Modifier(s)

Examples:

very quickly
quite carefully
extremely slowly
very carefully

An adverb phrase can also have other structures:

with great care
in the morning
after the meeting
with great confidence
Functions of an Adverb Phrase

An adverb phrase can tell us:

Example
He spoke with great confidence.
She arrived in the morning.
They waited near the gate.
He went there to meet his friend.
She is very happy.
How to Identify an Adverb Phrase

Look for a group of words that gives more information about a verb, adjective, or another adverb.

Example:

He completed the work with great care.

Adverb Phrase: with great care
Describes: completed
Function: Tells how he completed the work.
How an Adverb Phrase Adds Information

An adverb phrase adds details about how, when, where, or why an action happens.

Simple:

He worked.

More information:

He worked with great care.

Here:

worked → action
with great care → tells how he worked

Another example:

Simple:

She arrived.

More information:

She arrived early in the morning.

Here:

arrived → action
early in the morning → tells when she arrived
Easy Rule

An adverb phrase gives more information about a verb, adjective, or another adverb.

Exam Tip

Ask: “How? When? Where? or Why?” If the phrase answers one of these questions about the action, it may be an Adverb Phrase.

Gerund Phrase
Definition

English:
A gerund phrase is a group of words that begins with a gerund (-ing form of a verb) and works like a noun in a sentence.

Urdu:
ایسے الفاظ کے مجموعے کو اسمِ مصدر فقرہ (Gerund Phrase) کہتے ہیں جو جملے میں اسم (Noun) کا کام کرے اور عموماً فعل کی ing شکل (Gerund) سے شروع ہو۔

Examples

Swimming in the morning is good for health.
صبح تیراکی کرنا صحت کے لیے اچھا ہے۔

I enjoy reading interesting books.
مجھے دلچسپ کتابیں پڑھنا پسند ہے۔

She likes helping poor people.
وہ غریب لوگوں کی مدد کرنا پسند کرتی ہے۔

In each example, the bold words begin with a gerund and work like a noun.

Common Structure

Gerund + Object / Modifier(s)

Examples:

reading books
playing football
helping poor people
studying English every day
walking in the park

A gerund phrase can contain:

Gerund + Object + Modifiers

Reading English books every day

Reading → Gerund
English books → Object
every day → Modifier
Functions of a Gerund Phrase

A gerund phrase can work as:

Example
Reading books improves vocabulary.
I enjoy reading books.
She is interested in learning English.
His favorite activity is playing football.
How to Identify a Gerund Phrase

Look for a group of words that:

Begins with an -ing form of a verb.
The -ing word acts like a noun.
The whole group works as a noun in the sentence.

Example:

Learning English every day improves your skills.

Gerund Phrase: Learning English every day
Gerund: Learning
Object: English
Modifier: every day
Function: Subject
How a Gerund Phrase Adds Information

A gerund phrase turns an action into a noun idea and can add details about that action.

Simple:

Reading is useful.

More information:

Reading English books every day is useful.

Here:

Reading → Gerund
English books → tells what is being read
every day → tells when/how often
The whole phrase works as the subject.

Another example:

Simple:

I enjoy cooking.

More information:

I enjoy cooking delicious meals for my family.

Here:

cooking → Gerund
delicious meals → tells what is being cooked
for my family → tells for whom
Easy Rule

Gerund Phrase = Gerund (-ing) + other words, working like a noun.

Exam Tip

Do not identify every -ing word as a gerund. Check its function. If the -ing form works like a noun, it is a gerund.

Compare:

Swimming every morning is healthy. → Gerund Phrase (noun function)
The boy is swimming in the pool. → Verb Phrase (part of the verb)

Infinitive Phrase
Definition

English:
An infinitive phrase is a group of words that begins with to + base verb and works as a noun, adjective, or adverb in a sentence.

Urdu:
ایسے الفاظ کے مجموعے کو مصدر فقرہ (Infinitive Phrase) کہتے ہیں جو to کے ساتھ فعل کی پہلی شکل (Base Verb) سے شروع ہو کر اسم (Noun)، صفت (Adjective) یا حال (Adverb) کا کام کرے۔

Examples

To learn English takes time.
انگریزی سیکھنے میں وقت لگتا ہے۔

I want to buy a new phone.
میں ایک نیا فون خریدنا چاہتا ہوں۔

She went to the market to buy some vegetables.
وہ کچھ سبزیاں خریدنے کے لیے بازار گئی۔

In each example, the bold words begin with an infinitive and work together as a unit.

Common Structure

to + Base Verb + Object / Modifier(s)

Examples:

to read books
to learn English
to win the match
to help poor people
to study hard for the exam

Example:

to study English every day

to → infinitive marker
study → base verb
English → object
every day → modifier
Functions of an Infinitive Phrase

An infinitive phrase can work as:

Example
To learn English is important.
I have a book to read.
She went to the library to study.
How to Identify an Infinitive Phrase

Look for:

to + base verb
The words that follow it and complete the phrase.
Check what function the whole phrase performs.

Example:

She went to the market to buy some vegetables.

Infinitive Phrase: to buy some vegetables
Infinitive: to buy
Object: some vegetables
Function: Adverb — tells why she went to the market.
How an Infinitive Phrase Adds Information

An infinitive phrase can add information about an action, purpose, or thing.

Simple:

She went to the market.

More information:

She went to the market to buy some vegetables.

Here:

went → main action
to buy some vegetables → tells why she went

Another example:

Simple:

I need a book.

More information:

I need a book to read during the journey.

Here:

book → noun
to read during the journey → tells what the book is for
Easy Rule

Infinitive Phrase = to + Base Verb + other words

Exam Tip

Find “to + base verb” first, then check the function of the whole group.

Compare:

I want to learn English. → Infinitive Phrase
She went there to meet her friend. → Infinitive Phrase
To exercise regularly is beneficial. → Infinitive Phrase

Noun Phrase
Definition

English:
A noun phrase is a group of words that works like a noun in a sentence.

Urdu:
ایسے الفاظ کے مجموعے کو اسمی فقرہ (Noun Phrase) کہتے ہیں جو جملے میں اسم (Noun) کا کام کرے۔

Examples

The little boy is playing.
چھوٹا لڑکا کھیل رہا ہے۔

I bought a new laptop.
میں نے ایک نیا لیپ ٹاپ خریدا۔

She is a talented teacher.
وہ ایک قابل استاد ہے۔

In each example, the bold words work like a noun.

Common Structure

Determiner + Adjective(s) + Noun + Modifier

Examples:

the smart student
a beautiful garden
the three intelligent students in my class

Note: A noun phrase does not always contain all these parts.

Examples:

students
my friend
the boy
the very intelligent student
Functions of a Noun Phrase
Example
The little girl cried.
I met the new teacher.
Ali is a good student.
She sat beside the old man.
How to Identify a Noun Phrase

Look for the main noun and the words that describe or identify it.

Example:

The very intelligent student in my class won the prize.

Noun Phrase: The very intelligent student in my class
Head noun: student
Function: Subject
How a Noun Phrase Adds Information

A noun phrase adds information by giving more details about a noun.

Simple:

I saw a man.

More information:

I saw a tall man with a long beard.

Here:

man → main noun
tall → describes the man
with a long beard → gives more information about the man

Another example:

Simple:

She bought a dress.

More information:

She bought a beautiful red dress for the party.

Here:

dress → main noun
beautiful, red → describe the dress
for the party → gives additional information
Easy Rule

A noun phrase makes a noun more specific by adding words that describe or identify it.

Exam Tip

If a group of words works like a noun, it is a Noun Phrase.

Participle Phrase
Definition

English:
A participle phrase is a group of words that begins with a present participle (-ing) or past participle (-ed, -en, etc.) and works like an adjective to describe a noun or pronoun.

Urdu:
ایسے الفاظ کے مجموعے کو وصفی فعلی فقرہ (Participial Phrase) کہتے ہیں جو اسم (Noun) یا ضمیر (Pronoun) کی وضاحت کرے اور فعل کی وصفی شکل (Participle) سے شروع ہو۔

Examples

The boy wearing a blue shirt is my brother.
نیلی قمیض پہنے ہوئے لڑکا میرا بھائی ہے۔

Tired after the long journey, the travelers rested.
طویل سفر کے بعد تھکے ہوئے، مسافروں نے آرام کیا۔

The books written by Shakespeare are famous.
شیکسپیئر کی لکھی ہوئی کتابیں مشہور ہیں۔

In each example, the bold phrase describes a noun or pronoun.

Common Structure

Participle + Object / Modifier(s)

Examples:

wearing a blue shirt
running very quickly
tired after the journey
written by Shakespeare
broken by the child

A participle phrase can contain:

Participle + Object + Modifiers

Wearing a blue shirt

Wearing → Present participle
a blue shirt → Object

Written by Shakespeare

Written → Past participle
by Shakespeare → Modifier
Functions of a Participle Phrase

A participle phrase mainly works as an adjective.

Example
The girl wearing a red dress is my sister.
Feeling tired, he went to bed.
The car damaged in the accident was repaired.
How to Identify a Participle Phrase

Look for a group of words that:

Begins with a present participle (-ing) or past participle.
Describes a noun or pronoun.
Gives additional information about that noun or pronoun.

Example:

The man standing near the door is my teacher.

Participle Phrase: standing near the door
Participle: standing
Describes: man
Function: Adjective
How a Participle Phrase Adds Information

A participle phrase adds descriptive information about a noun or pronoun without creating a separate sentence.

Simple:

The girl won the race.

More information:

The girl wearing a blue dress won the race.

Here:

girl → main noun
wearing a blue dress → describes the girl
The phrase tells us which girl.

Another example:

Simple:

The car was repaired.

More information:

The car damaged in the accident was repaired.

Here:

car → main noun
damaged in the accident → describes the car
The phrase tells us which car.
Easy Rule

Participle Phrase = Participle + other words, working like an adjective.

Exam Tip

If a participle phrase describes a noun or pronoun, it is functioning as an adjective.

Compare:

The boy wearing a blue shirt is my brother. → Participle Phrase (describes boy)
The boy is wearing a blue shirt. → Verb Phrase (is wearing is the verb)

Prepositional Phrase
Definition

English:
A prepositional phrase is a group of words that begins with a preposition and ends with its object.

Urdu:
ایسے الفاظ کے مجموعے کو حرفِ جار کا فقرہ (Prepositional Phrase) کہتے ہیں جو حرفِ جار (Preposition) سے شروع ہو اور اس کے مفعول (Object) پر ختم ہو۔

Examples

The book is on the table.
کتاب میز پر ہے۔

She walked through the park.
وہ پارک میں سے گزرتی ہوئی چلی۔

I met him after the class.
میں اس سے کلاس کے بعد ملا۔

In each example, the bold words begin with a preposition and form a complete phrase.

Common Structure

Preposition + Object

Examples:

in the room
on the table
under the chair
with my friend
after the class
near the school

The object of the preposition can itself be a noun phrase:

in the large classroom

in → Preposition
the large classroom → Object of the preposition
Functions of a Prepositional Phrase

A prepositional phrase can:

Example
The keys are on the table.
We arrived after the class.
He walked toward the door.
The girl in the blue dress is my sister.
He spoke with confidence.
How to Identify a Prepositional Phrase

Look for a group of words that starts with a preposition and includes its object.

Example:

The students are sitting under the tree.

Prepositional Phrase: under the tree
Preposition: under
Object: tree
Function: Shows place
How a Prepositional Phrase Adds Information

A prepositional phrase adds information about place, time, direction, manner, or relationship.

Simple:

The book is.

More information:

The book is on the table.

Here:

book → noun
is → verb
on the table → tells where the book is

Another example:

Simple:

We arrived.

More information:

We arrived after the meeting.

Here:

arrived → action
after the meeting → tells when we arrived
Easy Rule

Prepositional Phrase = Preposition + Object

Exam Tip

Find the preposition first. Then include the preposition, its object, and any words modifying the object.

Example:

She sat on the wooden chair.

The complete prepositional phrase is on the wooden chair, not just on or chair.

Verb Phrase
Definition

English:
A verb phrase is a group of words that works together as the verb in a sentence.

Urdu:
ایسے الفاظ کے مجموعے کو فعلی فقرہ (Verb Phrase) کہتے ہیں جو جملے میں فعل (Verb) کا کام کرے اور عمل یا حالت کو ظاہر کرے۔

Examples

is playing football.
فٹبال کھیل رہا ہے۔

She has finished her work.
اس نے اپنا کام مکمل کر لیا ہے۔

They will be traveling tomorrow.
وہ کل سفر کر رہے ہوں گے۔

In each example, the bold words work together as the verb of the sentence.

Common Structure

Main Verb + Helping Verb(s) + Other Verb Forms

Examples:

is playing
has finished
will be traveling
has been studying

Note: A verb phrase may contain one or more helping verbs with a main verb.

Examples:

is working
was sleeping
has arrived
will have completed
could have been waiting
Functions of a Verb Phrase

A verb phrase can:

Example
She is writing a letter.
He has been ill for two days.
They will have finished the work.
You should study harder.
How to Identify a Verb Phrase

Look for the main verb and any helping verbs that work with it.

Example:

She has been studying English for two hours.

Verb Phrase: has been studying
Main verb: studying
Helping verbs: has, been
Function: Shows an ongoing action
How a Verb Phrase Adds Information

A verb phrase gives more information about an action or state, such as time, duration, possibility, ability, or necessity.

Simple:

She studies English.

More information:

She has been studying English for two hours.

Here:

studies → shows the action
has been studying → shows the action has continued over a period of time
for two hours → gives the duration

Another example:

Simple:

They travel.

More information:

They will be traveling tomorrow.

Here:

travel → shows the action
will be traveling → shows a future ongoing action
tomorrow → gives the time
Easy Rule

A verb phrase is a group of words that works together to show an action, state, or condition.

Exam Tip

Find the main verb and the helping verbs that work with it. Together, they form the Verb Phrase.

content.introduction: Future tense passive constructions are straightforward but require careful use of 'will be' or 'will have been'. Future Continuous and Future Perfect Continuous passive forms are not used in standard English. CSS and PMS exams frequently test Simple Future passive and Future Perfect passive.
content.urduExplanation: Future Tenses میں Passive Voice بنانے کے دو اہم طریقے ہیں۔ Simple Future میں 'will be + V3' یا 'shall be + V3' آتا ہے، جیسے 'She will write the letter' → 'The letter will be written by her'۔ Future Perfect میں 'will have been + V3' استعمال ہوتا ہے، جیسے 'They will have completed the project' → 'The project will have been completed by them'۔ Future Continuous اور Future Perfect Continuous کا Passive Voice عام طور پر نہیں بنایا جاتا اور انہیں امتحانات میں passive میں تبدیل کرنے کی کوشش نہیں کرنی چاہیے۔ 'Going to' کا Passive 'is/am/are going to be + V3' کی شکل میں بنتا ہے، جیسے 'They are going to build a hospital' → 'A hospital is going to be built by them'۔
content.englishExplanation: Future tenses have two primary passive forms in standard English. Simple Future Passive uses 'will be + V3' (or 'shall be + V3' in formal British usage). Formula: New subject + will be + V3 + (by + agent). Future Perfect Passive uses 'will have been + V3', indicating completion of an action before a future point. Formula: New subject + will have been + V3 + (by + agent). 'Going to' future also has a passive: 'is/am/are going to be + V3'. Future Continuous ('will be + V-ing') and Future Perfect Continuous ('will have been + V-ing') do not have standard passive forms and are not tested in this form. Negative future passive: insert 'not' after 'will' → 'will not be + V3'; 'will not have been + V3'.

types.name: Simple Future Passive
types.description: Active: S + will + V1 + O → Passive: O + will be + V3 + by + agent. Example: 'The company will launch a new product.' → 'A new product will be launched by the company.'

types.name: Future Perfect Passive
types.description: Active: S + will have + V3 + O → Passive: O + will have been + V3 + by + agent. Example: 'She will have finished the report by Monday.' → 'The report will have been finished by her by Monday.'

types.name: 'Going to' Future Passive
types.description: Active: S + is/am/are going to + V1 + O → Passive: O + is/am/are going to be + V3 + by + agent. Example: 'They are going to renovate the office.' → 'The office is going to be renovated by them.'

types.name: Future Continuous & Future Perfect Continuous (No Passive)
types.description: Future Continuous ('will be V-ing') and Future Perfect Continuous ('will have been V-ing') do not form standard passive constructions. Avoid converting them to passive.

types.name: Negative Simple Future Passive
types.description: Active: S + will not + V1 + O → Passive: O + will not be + V3 + by + agent. Example: 'He will not sign the document.' → 'The document will not be signed by him.'

rules: Simple Future passive: will be + V3. 'Will' is invariable for all subjects.
Future Perfect passive: will have been + V3. The time reference is retained after the verb phrase.
'Going to' future passive: is/am/are going to be + V3.
Future Continuous and Future Perfect Continuous do not have standard passive forms — do not attempt to passivise them.
Negative future passive: 'will not be + V3'; the contraction 'won't be + V3' is also acceptable in informal contexts.
The past participle (V3) must be correct regardless of the future auxiliary used.
Time expressions ('by next Monday', 'soon', 'before noon') are retained in the passive sentence.

examples.text: Active: The government will build a new highway. / Passive: A new highway will be built by the government.
examples.note: Simple Future passive: 'will build' → 'will be built'. 'A new highway' becomes the subject.

examples.text: Active: She will have submitted the report by Friday. / Passive: The report will have been submitted by her by Friday.
examples.note: Future Perfect passive: 'will have submitted' → 'will have been submitted'. 'She' → 'her'. Time phrase retained.

examples.text: Active: They are going to announce the results tomorrow. / Passive: The results are going to be announced by them tomorrow.
examples.note: 'Going to' passive: 'are going to announce' → 'are going to be announced'.

examples.text: Active: The company will not refund the money. / Passive: The money will not be refunded by the company.
examples.note: Negative Simple Future: 'will not refund' → 'will not be refunded'.

examples.text: Active: Scientists will have discovered a cure by 2030. / Passive: A cure will have been discovered by scientists by 2030.
examples.note: Future Perfect: 'will have discovered' → 'will have been discovered'. Time phrase 'by 2030' retained.

commonMistakes.wrong: The letter will written by her.
commonMistakes.right: The letter will be written by her.
commonMistakes.note: The auxiliary 'be' cannot be omitted in Simple Future passive. Must have 'will be + V3'.

commonMistakes.wrong: The project will have been complete by the team.
commonMistakes.right: The project will have been completed by the team.
commonMistakes.note: After 'will have been', the past participle V3 is required: 'complete' → 'completed'.

commonMistakes.wrong: The report will be being written by her.
commonMistakes.right: Rephrase: The report will be written by her. (Future Continuous has no standard passive.)
commonMistakes.note: Future Continuous passive is not standard. Use Simple Future passive instead.

commonMistakes.wrong: A hospital will going to be built by them.
commonMistakes.right: A hospital is going to be built by them.
commonMistakes.note: 'Going to' passive uses 'is/am/are going to be + V3', not 'will going to be'.

practice.question: Change to passive: 'The authorities will announce the decision tomorrow.'
options: The decision will be announced by the authorities tomorrow.
The decision will have been announced by the authorities tomorrow.
The decision is announced by the authorities tomorrow.
The decision would be announced by the authorities tomorrow.
practice.explanation: Simple Future passive: 'will announce' → 'will be announced'. Time adverb 'tomorrow' is retained. Option a is correct.

practice.question: Change to passive: 'She will have completed the task before noon.'
options: The task will be completed by her before noon.
The task has been completed by her before noon.
The task will have been completed by her before noon.
The task had been completed by her before noon.
practice.explanation: Future Perfect passive: 'will have completed' → 'will have been completed'. 'She' → 'her'. Time phrase retained. Option c is correct.

practice.question: Active: 'They are going to repair the road.' Which passive is correct?
options: The road will be repaired by them.
The road is going to be repaired by them.
The road is going to been repaired by them.
The road was going to be repaired by them.
practice.explanation: 'Going to' passive: 'are going to repair' → 'is going to be repaired'. 'Road' is singular; 'is'. Option b is correct.

quiz.question: Which passive form is correct for Simple Future tense?
quiz.explanation: Simple Future passive requires 'will be + V3'. Option a omits 'be'; option c has wrong form; option d is Future Perfect passive.

quiz.question: Active: 'Scientists will have found a vaccine.' Correct passive: ___
options: A vaccine will be found by scientists.
A vaccine has been found by scientists.
A vaccine will have been found by scientists.
A vaccine would have been found by scientists.
quiz.explanation: Future Perfect active 'will have found' → Future Perfect passive 'will have been found'. Option c is correct.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly converts Future Continuous to passive?
options: The project will be being finished by them.
The project will have been finished by them.
The project will be finished by them. (Rephrase — Future Continuous has no standard passive.)
The project was being finished by them.
quiz.explanation: Future Continuous ('will be finishing') has no standard passive form. The best approach is to rephrase as Simple Future passive: 'will be finished'.

content.summary: Future tense passives use: Simple Future → will be + V3; Future Perfect → will have been + V3; 'Going to' future → is/am/are going to be + V3. Future Continuous and Future Perfect Continuous have no standard passive forms. Always retain time expressions and use the correct past participle (V3).

content.introduction: Imperative sentences express commands, orders, requests, or advice. They have no stated subject — the subject 'you' is implied. Converting imperative sentences to passive voice is a unique and frequently tested skill in Pakistani competitive exams.
content.urduExplanation: Imperative Sentences وہ جملے ہوتے ہیں جن میں حکم، درخواست یا مشورہ دیا جاتا ہے، اور ان کا Subject 'you' چھپا ہوتا ہے۔ ان کا Passive بنانے کے دو طریقے ہیں: پہلا طریقہ: 'Let + Object + be + V3'، جیسے 'Open the door' → 'Let the door be opened'۔ دوسرا طریقہ: 'You are requested/advised/ordered to + V1 + Object'، جیسے 'Please sit down' → 'You are requested to sit down'۔ منفی حکم (Don't/Never) کی صورت میں: 'Let + Object + not + be + V3'، جیسے 'Don't waste time' → 'Let time not be wasted'۔ یاد رہے کہ Imperative کا Subject 'you' Passive میں عام طور پر ظاہر نہیں ہوتا۔
content.englishExplanation: Imperative sentences are commands or requests where the subject 'you' is understood but not stated. Because there is no explicit object that becomes the subject in the usual way, imperative passives use two specialised patterns. Pattern 1 – 'Let + object + be + V3': This is the primary exam-accepted form. The object of the active command becomes the focus, introduced by 'let'. Example: 'Shut the window.' → 'Let the window be shut.' Pattern 2 – 'You are requested/advised/ordered/told to + V1 + (object)': Used when expressing polite requests or formal orders. Example: 'Please submit your forms.' → 'You are requested to submit your forms.' Negative imperatives ('Do not', 'Never', 'Don't') are converted as: 'Let + object + not + be + V3' or 'You are advised/requested not to + V1'. Example: 'Don't litter the streets.' → 'Let the streets not be littered.' OR 'You are requested not to litter the streets.' The choice of 'requested', 'advised', 'ordered', or 'told' depends on the tone and context of the original command.

types.name: Pattern 1: Let + Object + be + V3
types.description: The primary passive form for imperatives. Active: 'V1 + object.' → Passive: 'Let + object + be + V3.' Example: 'Close the door.' → 'Let the door be closed.'

types.name: Pattern 2: You are requested/advised/ordered to + V1
types.description: Used for polite or formal requests. Example: 'Please help the poor.' → 'You are requested to help the poor.' OR 'The poor should be helped.'

types.name: Negative Imperative Passive (Pattern 1)
types.description: Active: 'Do not / Never + V1 + object.' → Passive: 'Let + object + not + be + V3.' Example: 'Don't waste water.' → 'Let water not be wasted.'

types.name: Negative Imperative Passive (Pattern 2)
types.description: Active: 'Do not + V1 + object.' → Passive: 'You are requested/advised not to + V1 + object.' Example: 'Do not make noise.' → 'You are requested not to make noise.'

types.name: Choosing the Right Verb (requested / advised / ordered / told)
types.description: Use 'requested' for polite requests, 'advised' for suggestions, 'ordered' or 'commanded' for strong directives, 'told' for instructions.

rules: The primary passive of an imperative is: Let + object + be + V3.
An alternative form is: You are requested/advised/ordered/told to + V1 + (object).
For negative imperatives ('Do not/Never + V1'): Let + object + not + be + V3 OR You are requested/advised not to + V1.
The implied subject 'you' is NOT written as 'by you' in the passive of imperatives — it is omitted.
Select 'requested', 'advised', 'ordered', or 'told' based on the strength and formality of the original command.
If the imperative has no direct object (e.g., 'Go away', 'Sit down'), it generally cannot be passivised using Pattern 1; use Pattern 2 instead.
The past participle (V3) must be correctly formed after 'be' in Pattern 1.

examples.text: Active: Open the window. / Passive: Let the window be opened.
examples.note: Pattern 1: 'the window' becomes subject of 'let' construction; 'open' → 'be opened'.

examples.text: Active: Help the poor. / Passive: Let the poor be helped. / OR: You are requested to help the poor.
examples.note: Both Pattern 1 and Pattern 2 are acceptable. Pattern 2 uses 'requested' for a polite tone.

examples.text: Active: Do not waste time. / Passive: Let time not be wasted. / OR: You are advised not to waste time.
examples.note: Negative imperative: 'not' is placed after 'Let + object' or after 'not to' in Pattern 2.

examples.text: Active: Never tell a lie. / Passive: Let a lie never be told. / OR: You are advised never to tell a lie.
examples.note: Adverb 'never' is retained and placed appropriately in the passive.

examples.text: Active: Please submit your application. / Passive: You are requested to submit your application.
examples.note: Polite imperative with 'please': use 'requested'. Pattern 2 is most natural here.

examples.text: Active: Follow the traffic rules. / Passive: Let the traffic rules be followed. / OR: You are ordered to follow the traffic rules.
examples.note: Both patterns work; 'ordered' suits a directive context.

commonMistakes.note: After 'be' in passive, the past participle V3 is required: 'close' (V1) → 'closed' (V3).
The object must immediately follow 'let': 'Let + object (time) + not + be + V3'.

commonMistakes.wrong: You are requested to not make noise.
commonMistakes.right: You are requested not to make noise.
commonMistakes.note: In formal English, 'not' precedes 'to' in the infinitive: 'not to make', not 'to not make'.

commonMistakes.wrong: Let the children be played. (Active: 'Play, children!')
commonMistakes.right: Let the children play. (This is already a 'let' sentence, not a passive.)
commonMistakes.note: When the imperative begins with 'Let + noun + V1', it is already a permission/suggestion — do not add 'be' unless converting to passive.

practice.question: Change to passive: 'Clean the room immediately.'
options: Let the room be cleaned immediately.
Let the room be clean immediately.
The room must be cleaned immediately.
You are advised to clean the room immediately.
practice.explanation: Pattern 1 imperative passive: 'Let + the room + be + cleaned'. V3 of 'clean' is 'cleaned'. Adverb 'immediately' is retained. Both a and d are acceptable but a is the primary exam answer. Option a is the most standard Pattern 1 response.

practice.question: Change to passive: 'Do not park your car here.'
options: Let your car not parked here.
Let your car not be parked here.
You are requested to not park your car here.
Your car must not be parked here.
practice.explanation: Negative imperative Pattern 1: 'Let + your car + not + be + parked'. V3 of 'park' is 'parked'. Option b is correct. Option c has incorrect infinitive placement.

practice.question: Which is the most appropriate passive for: 'Please respect your teachers.'?
options: You are requested to respect your teachers.
Both a and b are acceptable.
practice.explanation: Both Pattern 1 ('Let your teachers be respected') and Pattern 2 ('You are requested to respect your teachers') are grammatically correct passives for a polite imperative. Option d is correct.

quiz.question: Identify the correct passive of: 'Never break the law.'
options: The law should never be broken.
Let the law never be broken.
Let the law not be broken never.
You are requested to never break the law.
quiz.explanation: Imperative Pattern 1: 'Let + the law + never + be + broken'. 'Never' is placed before 'be'. Option b is the most standard exam answer.

quiz.question: Active: 'Switch off the lights before leaving.' Passive (Pattern 1): ___
options: Let the lights be switched off before leaving.
Let the lights be switch off before leaving.
Let the lights are switched off before leaving.
The lights should be switched off before leaving.
quiz.explanation: Pattern 1: 'Let + the lights + be + switched off'. V3 of 'switch off' is 'switched off'. Time phrase retained. Option a is correct.

quiz.question: Which of the following is the Pattern 2 passive of: 'Obey the orders.'?
options: You are ordered to obey the orders.
The orders are to be obeyed.
Orders must be obeyed by you.
quiz.explanation: Pattern 2: 'You are ordered/requested to + V1 + object'. 'Obey the orders' → 'You are ordered to obey the orders.' Option b is Pattern 2.

content.summary: Imperative sentences convert to passive using two patterns: Pattern 1 – 'Let + object + be + V3' (primary form); Pattern 2 – 'You are requested/advised/ordered to + V1 + object'. Negative imperatives use 'Let + object + not + be + V3' or 'You are advised/requested not to + V1'. The implied subject 'you' is not written as agent in imperative passives.

content.introduction: Interrogative sentences (questions) can be converted to passive voice, but the question structure must be preserved. Yes/No questions (using auxiliaries) and Wh-questions each have their own passive conversion pattern. The most tested form on competitive exams is the 'Who/Whom' question conversion.
content.urduExplanation: سوالیہ جملوں کو Passive Voice میں تبدیل کرنا ذرا مختلف ہوتا ہے لیکن قابل فہم ہے۔ Yes/No سوالات میں Auxiliary Verb (helping verb) کو آگے رکھا جاتا ہے، جیسے 'Did she write the letter?' → 'Was the letter written by her?'۔ Wh-Questions میں Wh-Word کو آگے رکھا جاتا ہے، جیسے 'What did he buy?' → 'What was bought by him?'۔ خاص اہمیت 'Who' سوالات کی ہے: 'Who wrote this letter?' → 'By whom was this letter written?' یا 'Who was this letter written by?'۔ یاد رہے کہ Passive Question میں بھی سوالیہ شکل (inversion) برقرار رہتی ہے۔
content.englishExplanation: Interrogative passive sentences maintain the question word order: auxiliary verb before subject. For Yes/No questions, the structure is: Passive auxiliary (is/are/was/were/will be + V3) + new subject + (by + agent) + ? For Wh-questions (what, which, when, where, why, how), the Wh-word is placed first, followed by the passive auxiliary inversion. The most important special case is 'Who' questions: 'Who' as subject of an active question converts to 'By whom' in passive (formal) or 'Who ... by?' (informal). Formula for 'Who' questions: Active: 'Who + V2 + object?' → Passive: 'By whom + was/were + object + V3?' For 'Whom' as object in active: 'Whom did she invite?' → 'Who was invited by her?' — here 'whom' (old object) becomes the new subject 'who'. The tense of the passive auxiliary must match the tense of the original active question.

types.name: Yes/No Question Passive
types.description: Active: Auxiliary + subject + V1 + object? → Passive: Passive auxiliary (was/were/is/are + V3) + new subject + by + agent? Example: 'Did he solve the problem?' → 'Was the problem solved by him?'

types.name: Wh-Question Passive (Object Wh-word)
types.description: Active: Wh-word (as object) + auxiliary + subject + V1? → Passive: Wh-word + passive auxiliary + new subject + V3 + by + agent? Example: 'What did she buy?' → 'What was bought by her?'

types.name: 'Who' as Subject (Active) → 'By whom' (Passive)
types.description: Active: 'Who + V2 + object?' → Passive: 'By whom + was/were + object + V3?' (formal) OR 'Who was [object] V3 by?' (informal). Example: 'Who wrote this letter?' → 'By whom was this letter written?'

types.name: 'Whom' as Object (Active) → 'Who' as Subject (Passive)
types.description: Active: 'Whom did + subject + V1?' → Passive: 'Who + was/were + V3 + by + agent?' Example: 'Whom did the teacher punish?' → 'Who was punished by the teacher?'

types.name: Wh-Question with Subject Wh-word (What/Which)
types.description: Active: 'What + V2 + object?' → Passive retains 'What' and inverts: 'What + was/were + V3 + by + agent?' Example: 'What surprised him?' → 'By what was he surprised?' (formal) or 'What was he surprised by?'

rules: The question form (inversion of auxiliary and subject) must be preserved in the passive.
Yes/No questions: replace active auxiliary with passive auxiliary (was/were/is/are + V3) and maintain question order.
'Who' as active subject → 'By whom' at the start of the passive question (formal) or 'Who ... by?' (informal).
'Whom' as active object → becomes 'Who' (new subject) at the start of the passive question.
For Wh-questions where the Wh-word is the object, keep it at the front and convert the rest: 'What did he bring?' → 'What was brought by him?'
Tense of the passive auxiliary must match the tense of the original question auxiliary.
